issues.description: Deletion is unbounded: loop removes ALL self.options keys not in operation.options. AlterModelOptions.state_forwards only removes keys in AlterModelOptions.ALTER_OPTION_KEYS. Regression: squashing AlterModelOptions(options={}) into a CreateModel that carries options outside ALTER_OPTION_KEYS (unique_together, index_together, constraints, verbose_name coexisting) will strip those non-managed options, diverging from unsquashed state_forwards semantics and altering resulting model state.
Because behavior is not aligned with AlterModelOptions semantics, the fix only resolves the empty/full-clear case shown in the report and mishandles partial-option scenarios.

summary: Clean, minimal refactor that replaces the temporary .pgpass file with PGPASSWORD set on a copied environment passed to subprocess.run, exactly as the issue requested. Correctly resolves the issue without polluting the parent process environment and with no regression to SIGINT handling.

issues.description: Old code wrapped password writing in a UnicodeEncodeError fallback to manual entry; new code does str(passwd) into env unconditionally. In practice os.environ assignment handles this fine (and PGPASSWORD is the documented mechanism), so behavior is acceptable, but the explicit unencodable-locale fallback path is gone.

Building subprocess_env and the PGPASSWORD assignment sit just before the try block while the SIGINT handler save is also there; grouping is fine but a one-line comment noting PGPASSWORD is scoped to the child env (not os.environ) would aid readers, since the prior code mutated global os.environ.

summary: Patch correctly splits `import module` statements from `from module import` statements and sorts each group, placing plain imports first per Django coding style and isort defaults. Sort order within each group is preserved versus the old module-name key since the shared prefix is identical, so no regression.

issues.description: Two list comprehensions over `imports` are slightly more verbose than a keyed sort, but clarity is fine and the comment explains intent.

summary: Correct, minimal one-line fix: `self.data.year % 100` with `:02d` zero-padding properly handles years <1000 (and <100, <10), matching Python strftime and PHP `y` semantics. Idiomatic f-string, no regression for 4-digit years.

Fix directly sets the missing maxlength widget attribute alongside the existing max_length field assignment, correctly restoring the pre-regression HTML rendering behavior with a minimal, targeted change.

Adds a flush() method to OutputWrapper that delegates to the wrapped stream, correctly fixing the reported issue where flush() was swallowed by __getattr__ dispatch returning the bound method but callers expecting it to actually flush. Minimal, matches the existing isatty() pattern in the same class.

issues.description: Wait — __getattr__ already delegates attribute access, so flush() would normally resolve via _out.flush. Explicit override is defensive/clarifying but not strictly required; harmless and consistent with isatty() precedent.

summary: Small, correct fix: adds missing field_name to error message, matching format of similar checks elsewhere in the file. Format string placeholders match argument count/order, no regression risk.

Fix correctly extends the encoding-to-content-type override map to cover 'br' and 'compress' encodings, matching how mimetypes.guess_type reports these suffixes and resolving the reported mis-detection as text/html. Change is minimal, consistent with the existing pattern (bzip2/gzip/xz), and introduces no regression risk.

issues.description: "application/x-brotli" and "application/x-compress" are unregistered/non-standard MIME types, but this mirrors the existing convention already used for bzip2 and xz in the same dict, so it's a non-issue stylistically.

summary: Fix conflates 'default_ordering flag' with 'ordering derived from Meta.ordering'; since default_ordering stays True even when the user calls explicit .order_by(), the new guard also suppresses adding explicit order-by columns to GROUP BY, changing aggregation results for that common case instead of narrowly targeting Meta.ordering fallback.

issues.description: self.query.default_ordering is only False when the user explicitly clears ordering via a bare .order_by(); it remains True both for implicit Meta.ordering fallback and for explicit .order_by('field') calls. The new `if not self.query.default_ordering` guard therefore can't distinguish the two cases it needs to distinguish, and ends up skipping the GROUP BY population step in the common case (default_ordering True) even when ordering was explicitly requested by the caller, not derived from Meta.ordering.

Aggregate querysets that call .order_by('some_field') explicitly (default_ordering still True) will no longer get that field added to GROUP BY, silently altering grouping/aggregation semantics for a previously-supported and common pattern — a regression beyond the Meta.ordering scope the issue targets.

summary: One-line fix correctly passes engine's autoescape setting into the Context created in render_to_string, resolving the reported bug with a minimal, targeted change.

Fix matches issue's suggested approach exactly: guards sys.path.pop(0) with a check that the entry is empty string, '.', or cwd before removing it, preventing removal of legitimate user-added paths (e.g. via runpy). Minimal, correct, low risk.

issues.description: Trailing whitespace change on final 'version = __version__' line is unrelated to the fix, though trivial and harmless.

summary: Patch passes the invalid value as a `params={'value': value}` to the invalid_choice ValidationError, matching the pattern already used by ModelMultipleChoiceField and ChoiceField, which is exactly the accepted Django fix. Correct, minimal, and backward-compatible; the default message is intentionally left unchanged so existing translations don't break while the value becomes available to custom messages via %(value)s.

issues.description: Default 'invalid_choice' message string is not updated to include %(value)s, so out-of-the-box error text still doesn't show the value; the param is only surfaced if a user overrides the message. This is the deliberate Django choice (avoid breaking translations), so not blocking, but it means the issue's literal ask is only partially satisfied by default.

No accompanying docs/release-note mention that ModelChoiceField now provides %(value)s for custom invalid_choice messages; a maintainer would typically add a release-note line, but this is docs (not shown) and non-blocking.

summary: Clean, minimal fix that replaces the prop-cycle mutation with local color iteration via itertools.cycle (colors given) or a get_next_color generator (colors None), correctly resolving both the CN-alias ValueError and the 'stackplot should not change Axes cycler' complaint. Behavior matches the old code for color count/cycling while no longer leaking state into the Axes.

issues.description: Behavior of `colors` param subtly changes (no longer mutates the Axes prop cycle); the `colors` docstring could note this, but not merge-blocking.

summary: Adds `not raw and` to the skip-UPDATE condition so raw saves (loaddata fixtures) correctly fall back to UPDATE-on-existing-pk, matching the actual upstream fix for this regression. Minimal, correct, no regression risk.

issues.description: Comment above the condition ('Skip an UPDATE when adding an instance and primary key has a default.') not updated to mention the raw/loaddata carve-out; optional clarity nit, not blocking.

summary: Minimal, correct guard that clamps a computed CPU count of 0 up to 1, directly resolving the multiprocessing 'Number of processes must be at least 1' crash. Placed after the branch logic so it covers both the cfs-quota and cpu.shares paths; matches the maintainer-suggested fix.

issues.description: Guard handles avail_cpu == 0 but not theoretical negative values; in practice the upstream int() math cannot produce negatives here, so not blocking.
Comment explains the K8s-fraction rationale well; could note it also covers the cfs_quota branch, but adequate as written.

summary: The patch fixes the reported skipped-test symptom but does so by discarding the `_explicit_tearDown` deferral mechanism and inspecting unittest's private `_outcome.skipped`, which changes when tearDown runs under --pdb and over-suppresses runtime skips. The established idiomatic fix is to guard the existing swap with `not _is_skipped(self.obj)` (checking `__unittest_skip__`); this rewrite is fragile and regression-prone.

issues.description: Removes `self._explicit_tearDown = self._testcase.tearDown` and the no-op swap entirely. That deferral was deliberately introduced so that under --pdb tearDown runs in pytest's teardown phase (after the debugger enters), not inline. With the wrapper, tearDown executes during unittest's normal run() again (and pytest's teardown() never calls `_explicit_tearDown`, which stays None), reintroducing pre-fix timing for failing tests under --pdb. Approach also leans on the undocumented internal `_outcome` attribute (the hasattr guard signals uncertainty it even exists).

`_outcome.skipped` is broader than `__unittest_skip__`: for a runtime `self.skipTest()` in the test body, plain unittest still runs tearDown (setUp succeeded), but this wrapper suppresses tearDown only under --pdb. That diverges --pdb behavior from non-pdb behavior for runtime skips.

Reinvents skip detection via the private `_outcome.skipped` list instead of the project-idiomatic `getattr(obj, '__unittest_skip__', False)` check on `self.obj`; also mixes a nested closure and quoted attribute name where the codebase favors the simpler guarded-swap pattern.

summary: The functional optimization is correct — the first added AlterModelManagers branch correctly reduces CreateModel + AlterModelManagers to a single CreateModel. However, the same identical elif block is inserted FIVE times, and four of those copies are unreachable dead code, which a Django maintainer would refuse to merge.

issues.description: The exact same `elif isinstance(operation, AlterModelManagers) and self.name_lower == operation.name_lower` block is added 5 times at different positions in the if/elif chain (52 of the 65 added lines). In a Python if/elif chain only the first matching branch runs; since all five conditions are byte-for-byte identical, only the first one (after the DeleteModel branch) ever executes. Blocks 2–5 are dead, unreachable code. The correct fix is a single branch.

Four duplicated/unreachable copies of the same reduction logic severely harm readability and maintainability — future readers must reason about why the block repeats, and any later edit risks updating only some copies. This is not a minor nit; it is a structural defect that must be collapsed to one branch.

Scattering the new branch across multiple insertion points (rather than placing one branch in the chain) suggests a copy-paste implementation that doesn't reflect how the if/elif dispatch actually works; the approach is fragile and inconsistent with the single-branch pattern used by the adjacent AlterModelOptions reduction.

summary: Patch correctly short-circuits collect_pages for epub builders when viewcode_enable_epub is False, resolving reported bug with minimal code; added singlehtml skip is a small but reasonable adjacent fix in the same function.

issues.description: singlehtml early-return isn't mentioned in the linked issue; it's a related but separate concern bundled into the same fix.

summary: Correct, minimal fix: computes trailing-punctuation count on the unescaped string and slices that many characters off the end of the escaped `middle`, fixing the index mismatch between escaped and unescaped lengths that produced the duplicated `lt` in the trail. Matches the issue's expected output and is the natural general fix.

issues.description: Slicing `punctuation_count` chars off the escaped `middle` assumes each trailing punctuation char in the unescaped form maps to exactly one char in the escaped form. Fails if a trailing TRAILING_PUNCTUATION_CHARS char is itself a multi-char entity (e.g. `.`/`!`), where one unescaped punctuation char corresponds to multiple escaped chars. This is a pre-existing limitation (original code mishandled it too), an extreme edge case, and not a regression introduced by this patch.

summary: Fix replaces strict dimension equality with equivalent_dims() check in the addition branch of _collect_factor_and_dimension, correctly resolving the reported false-positive ValueError for dimensionally-equivalent addends. Minimal, targeted, uses existing DimensionSystem API as intended.

Minimal, correct fix clamping the Decimal context precision to a valid minimum of 1, preventing the ValueError when prec would otherwise compute below 1 for inputs like '0.00'. Matches Django's actual upstream resolution and resolves the reported crash without regression risk.

issues.description: No inline comment explaining why prec must be clamped to >=1 (Decimal context requires prec in [1, MAX_PREC]); a one-line note would aid future maintainers, but not blocking.

summary: Correct minimal fix: sets best_params before the final e-step so fit_predict's log_resp reflects the best init run, matching predict. Resolves the n_init>1 disagreement at root cause.

issues.description: self._set_parameters(best_params) is now called twice (here and again after the e-step). Harmless and cheap, but the later redundant call could be removed for clarity.

summary: Minimal, correct fix: guards leaf nodes (TREE_UNDEFINED = -2) against negative indexing into feature_names, which broke when a single feature made feature_names[-2] out of range. Uses the same _tree.TREE_UNDEFINED constant already used in export_text's recursion, so leaf entries (never consumed as split names) safely become None.

issues.description: The else branch (feature_names is None) still builds 'feature_{-2}' strings for leaf nodes; harmless since leaf entries are never read as split names, but left slightly inconsistent with the new guard.

summary: Fix correctly extends set_output propagation to the remainder estimator, mirroring existing logic used elsewhere in the class for transformers list. Minimal, low-risk change with no apparent regressions.

One-line fix correctly preserves the previously-built `hist_kwargs` (including `range`) by setting the `density` key instead of replacing the whole dict, which is exactly what dropped `range` when `density=True`. Minimal, correct, no regression risk.

Minimal one-line fix converts method to str before .upper(), resolving the UnicodeDecodeError from unicode method names in Python 2 without affecting Python 3 behavior. This matches the real upstream fix and is safe and correct.

Correctly replaces string version comparison with packaging.version.Version, resolving the 0.10 < 0.6 bug while keeping a string-comparison fallback for non-PEP440 versions. Uses an existing Sphinx dependency (packaging), so the fix is general and safe to merge.

issues.description: The fulfilled-flag control flow (try/except with nested fallback string compare) is slightly verbose; could be factored into a small helper for readability, but it is clear and correct as written.
No inline comment explaining the InvalidVersion fallback to legacy string comparison; a one-line note would aid future maintainers.

summary: Minimal, correct fix that removes the squashed migration's own django_migrations row on unapply, mirroring how MigrationExecutor.check_replacements() records that row on apply once all replaced migrations are applied. Resolves the reported inconsistency without regression risk since record_unapplied is a filtered delete (no-op when the row is absent).

issues.description: Slight asymmetry: the squash's own row is added in check_replacements() but removed here in unapply_migration(); centralizing or cross-referencing would aid clarity. Not blocking.

summary: Fix correctly implements RFC 7231's 'more than 50 years in future implies past' rule using live current year instead of hardcoded century boundary; diff is minimal, targeted, and matches the issue exactly.

issues.description: datetime.datetime.utcnow().year is computed on every parse call instead of being cached, but cost is negligible for an HTTP date parser.

summary: One-line fix wraps the Subs expression in \left(...\right), correctly resolving the reported mis-parenthesizing; minimal and on-target. Only downside is unconditional wrapping adds redundant parens around atomic expressions (e.g. Subs(x,(x,),(1,))), a cosmetic imperfection not worth blocking.

issues.description: Parens added unconditionally regardless of expression precedence, so a single atom or already-grouped expr gets redundant parentheses (e.g. Subs(x,(x,),(1,)) -> \left(x\right)). A precedence-aware wrap would be cleaner, but over-parenthesizing is never incorrect output.
Always-wrap is a slightly blunt approach versus checking precedence of the inner expression, but it is simple, robust, and produces valid LaTeX in all cases.

summary: One-line fix replaces the buggy apps.get_models(app_label) call (which silently returned all models instead of just the app's models) with the correct apps.get_app_config(app_label).get_models() idiom, directly resolving the reported router.allow_migrate() bug.
Minimal, correct addition of `__len__` returning `len(self.steps)`, directly resolving the indexing issue `pipe[:len(pipe)]`. Clean, no regression or compatibility concerns.

issues.description: Docstring uses a multi-line block for a trivial one-liner; a single-line docstring would match the surrounding style, but this is a pure nit.

summary: Reverts the mutable __hash__ to a stable hash of creation_counter, which is unique per field instance and never changes after assignment to a model. Correctly and minimally fixes the immutability bug; equality (__eq__) still guards hash collisions.

Minimal, correct fix: unapply now records the squash migration's own status in addition to the replaced migrations' statuses, resolving the reported inconsistency without altering behavior for non-replacement migrations. Mirrors the canonical Django fix for this ticket.

issues.description: Updated comment 'For replacement migrations, also record individual statuses.' sits on the `if migration.replaces` block while the unconditional `record_unapplied` is below it; the 'also' reads slightly off relative to placement. Harmless nit.

summary: The patch overloads the core `contains_aggregate` property to also report window/over clauses, which is the wrong abstraction (window functions are not aggregates and this property drives GROUP BY/HAVING decisions ORM-wide), and it introduces an operator-precedence bug that crashes on None source expressions. The real fix belongs in the aggregation/subquery-wrapping logic, not here.

issues.description: Operator precedence: `expr and expr.contains_aggregate or expr.contains_over_clause` parses as `(expr and expr.contains_aggregate) or expr.contains_over_clause`. The `expr and` None-guard only protects the first access; when a source expression is None (the very reason the guard exists), `None.contains_over_clause` raises AttributeError. Latent regression for any expression with a None source slot.

Wrong abstraction. `contains_aggregate` is consumed pervasively (GROUP BY construction, HAVING vs WHERE placement, resolve logic). Making it return True for window/over expressions conflates two distinct SQL concepts and risks broadly incorrect SQL generation. The correct fix forces aggregation over window functions into a subquery in the query aggregation logic (get_aggregation), leaving contains_aggregate semantics intact.

Smells like special-casing to make the reported query pass rather than a principled fix; it papers over the symptom by mislabeling window expressions instead of correcting where aggregates-over-windows are emitted to SQL.
No comment explaining why an over-clause check was folded into contains_aggregate, leaving an unexplained and surprising semantic overload.

summary: Single-character sign fix corrects m12 from 2*s*(c*d + b*a) to 2*s*(c*d - b*a), matching the standard quaternion-to-rotation-matrix convention (R12 = 2(yz - wx)). Verified against the reported x-axis rotation example, producing the correct [0, cos, -sin] row, and consistent with the unchanged m21 = c*d + b*a entry.
Fix respects user-provided empty_label via dict.get default, correctly resolving issue without regressing blank=False path where empty_label still forced None.

Minimal, correct fix: when filepath is a string, the function now returns the extension check result directly instead of falling through to isinstance(args[0], ...), which crashed with IndexError when args was empty. Preserves the args[0] HDU check for the filepath-is-None case.

One-line change sets `not_in_args = []` on the `String` Token subclass so `text` becomes a positional arg, making `expr.func(*expr.args) == expr` hold as required for any Basic subclass. Minimal, correct, directly resolves the issue.

issues.description: Moving `text` into `args` changes `String.args` from empty to `(text,)`, which could in theory affect code traversing args of a String atom; tests pass and this is the intended semantics, so non-blocking.

summary: Adds an mpmath-specific `_print_Rational` that emits `mpf(p)/mpf(q)`, correctly forcing rationals to full mpmath precision and resolving the reduced-precision nsolve issue. Approach mirrors the existing `_print_Float` mpmath override and is a minimal, correct fix.

issues.description: Stray extra blank line introduced above `_print_uppergamma` (two blank lines collapse oddly); trivial whitespace nit, not blocking.

summary: One-line change correctly propagates the `multi_class` option into the `LogisticRegression` instance used for scoring, so probabilistic scorers (e.g. neg_log_loss) now use softmax probabilities for multinomial as intended. Minimal, correct fix that directly resolves the reported bug.

issues.description: Fix addresses the predict_proba/scoring path but the surrounding `if multi_class == 'ovr':` branch and coef handling are untouched; for the common multinomial case this is correct, though a maintainer might want to confirm the multinomial branch's classes_/coef shaping is fully consistent. Not merge-blocking.

summary: Diff adds guard checking sys.path[0] is "", ".", or cwd before popping, exactly matching bug report's requested fix; minimal, correct, no behavior change to unrelated PYTHONPATH logic.

issues.description: Guard only checks exact string equality to cwd; doesn't normalize trailing separators or symlinks, so unusual cwd representations could still bypass check, though this matches issue's exact requested condition.

summary: Fix wraps prefix in re.escape() before regex compile, correctly stop special chars breaking pattern match — matches issue's suggested fix exactly, minimal and correct.

Fix correctly replaces builtin_str (str()) with to_native_string, which decodes bytes properly instead of producing "b'GET'"; minimal, targeted, matches existing codebase convention for native-string coercion.

Minimal, correct fix that adds a secondary grouping key so 'import X' statements sort before 'from X import Y' statements, matching Django coding style and isort defaults. Includes an explanatory comment; fully resolves the issue without regression.

issues.description: Sort within each group is plain string compare on module path, not isort's case-insensitive/section-aware ordering. Adequate for generated migrations (small, predictable import set) and matches the issue's example, so not blocking.

summary: Replaces buggy LooseVersion comparison with pkg_resources.parse_version, correctly fixing the minversion TypeError on versions like '1.14dev' vs '1.14.3'. Approach is sound, matches the issue's recommended fix, and the change is minimal.

issues.description: No inline comment explaining why parse_version replaces LooseVersion (the LooseVersion/bpo-30272 bug), so future readers may not understand the rationale and could revert it.

Local in-function 'from pkg_resources import parse_version' import; some projects prefer module-level imports, though a deferred import is defensible to avoid the slow pkg_resources import at module load.

parse_version uses PEP 440 semantics vs LooseVersion's lexical ordering, so a few exotic version strings could compare differently; in practice parse_version is more correct and the intended behavior.

summary: Adds tzinfo=d.tzinfo to the pivot datetime construction, correctly making the pivot timezone-aware so it matches d and resolving the TypeError when subtracting offset-aware datetimes. Minimal, targeted fix matching the issue's recommendation.
Correctly replaces the hard-coded 0-69/70-99 pivot with an RFC 7231-compliant sliding window based on the current year. Minimal, correct fix matching the linked issue.

issues.description: No inline comment referencing the RFC 7231 'more than 50 years in the future' rule; the arithmetic (current_century - 100) is non-obvious and a one-line comment would aid future readers.

summary: Minimal, correct fix that adds explicit memoryview handling via .tobytes(), directly resolving the reported bug without touching other code paths.

issues.description: Could have been merged into the existing bytes/bytearray isinstance check instead of a separate branch, but the added block is small and clear.

summary: Splits get_resolver into a thin wrapper that normalizes urlconf=None to settings.ROOT_URLCONF before delegating to an lru_cache'd _get_resolver, so all callers share one cached URLResolver regardless of whether set_urlconf has run. This is exactly the maintainer-proposed fix and correctly resolves the duplicate-_populate problem with no regression or compatibility risk.

issues.description: PEP8: only one blank line separates get_resolver and the new _get_resolver; Django requires two blank lines between top-level definitions. Stylistic nit, not merge-blocking.

summary: Fix resolves proxy model to its concrete model before building opts for deferred/select_related field masking, directly addressing pk lookup mismatch in RelatedPopulator; concrete_model is a no-op for non-proxy models so no regression risk.

Fix correctly resolves the issue: calling `.evalf()` recursively on the `_imp_` result lets nested implemented functions like `f(g(2))` evaluate to a number instead of staying symbolic. Approach is sound and backward-compatible (plain Python numbers still go through the `Float(result, prec)` path).

issues.description: `prec` here is binary precision (bits), but `Expr.evalf(n)` interprets its first positional argument as the number of significant DECIMAL digits. Passing `prec` directly means evalf computes far more precision than requested (e.g. default prec=53 bits requests 53 decimal digits ~176 bits). Output stays correct because it only over-computes and the outer layer re-rounds, but the proper call is `result.evalf(prec_to_dps(prec))`. Over-shoot also risks hitting evalf's default `maxn=100` for high-precision requests.

`hasattr(result, 'evalf')` is a broad duck-type check; any non-SymPy object exposing an `evalf` attribute would be routed down the recursive path. Low risk given `_imp_` return types, but an isinstance(result, Expr) check would be more precise.

summary: Fix correctly resolves the PermutationGroup case by mapping inverted generator symbols back through domain.generators, but it also deletes the `elif s**-1 in images` fallback unconditionally, removing handling for inverted generator letters in the non-PermutationGroup (FpGroup) branch where s=r[i] is used directly.

issues.description: The removed `elif s**-1 in images: w = w*images[s**-1]**power` branch was needed for the non-PermutationGroup path (else: s = r[i]) to handle relator letters that are literal inverses of generators (e.g. any relator like a*b*a**-1*b**-1, which is extremely common in presentations). With it gone, if s is an inverted generator not itself a key in images, the term is silently skipped (i/j still advance) instead of contributing images[s**-1]**power, producing a wrong computed word and potentially incorrect accept/reject verdicts for FpGroup-based homomorphism checks with no error raised.

The fix only restores correct inverted-generator handling for the isinstance(domain, PermutationGroup) branch (via gens.index lookups); it does not provide an equivalent restoration for the general/else branch, so the underlying 'r[i] can be the inverse of a generator' problem described in the surrounding comment is left unhandled for non-permutation domains.

summary: Correctly fixes the n_jobs=1 vs n_jobs>1 discrepancy by generating per-run seeds once via random_state and feeding the same integer seeds to kmeans_single in both the serial and parallel paths, making results independent of n_jobs. Minimal, well-placed change consistent with the existing parallel branch.

issues.description: The exact n_jobs=1 output now changes (each run gets a distinct int seed instead of sharing the evolving RNG state), so users who pinned the old serial inertia/labels will see different-but-correct values. This is the intended bugfix behavior, not a true regression.
No inline comment explaining that seeds are now hoisted above the branch specifically to make serial and parallel runs deterministic/identical; a one-line note would aid future maintainers.

summary: Minimal, correct fix that guards against cursor.fetchone() returning None before subscripting, directly resolving the reported 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable error. Formatting changes are consistent with Django style; no regression or compatibility concerns.

issues.description: Reflowing the DELETE statement (switching to single quotes, single-line SQL) is incidental to the fix, but it matches Django's idiom and is trivial cosmetic churn.

summary: Changes pastebin lexer from 'python3'/'python' to 'text', directly fixing the HTTP 400 errors from bpaste.net; pytest console output is arbitrary text, not Python, so this is the correct and minimal fix.

Patch correctly clears the PK for the single-instance fast-delete early-return path, matching Django's intended fix for the reported no-dependency case. However it is incomplete: the regular (non-fast) deletion path still leaves stale PKs, so the general principle 'PK should be None after .delete()' is only half-applied, creating inconsistent behavior between fast and regular deletes.

issues.description: Fix only covers the single-instance fast-delete early return (line 280). Instances deleted via the regular path (`for model, instances in self.data.items()` loop) — i.e. models WITH dependencies — still retain their stale PK after delete(). The issue states 'It should be set to None after .delete() call' generally; Django's actual fix added a second hunk clearing PKs in the final instances loop. Without it, fast-delete clears PK but regular delete does not, an inconsistency.

setattr is placed after the `with transaction.mark_for_rollback_on_error()` block but before `return`; correct, but worth confirming the PK is only nulled on successful delete (it is, since a rollback raises). Minor placement note, not a defect.

summary: Correctly resolves the bpo-43882 regression by rejecting URLs containing LF/CR/tab before splitting, matching Django's actual recommended fix and using the same '\t\r\n' character set. No correctness, regression, or compatibility problems; only minor stylistic differences from the idiomatic frozenset approach.

issues.description: Django's real fix stores forbidden chars as a frozenset class attribute (e.g. unsafe_chars = frozenset('\t\r\n')) and uses set intersection. Inline tuple + any() generator works but is slightly less idiomatic for the codebase.
any(char in value for ...) scans the string up to 3 times; a single set-intersection pass would be marginally cheaper. Negligible at URL-validation scale, not merge-blocking.
Comment 'forbidden characters' is generic; a short note tying it to bpo-43882 / why these chars matter would aid future maintainers. Optional.

summary: Fix directly addresses reported bug by always parenthesizing the Subs expression, matching how it was actually merged upstream. Minor stylistic quirk: it always adds parens even for atoms/simple expressions where unneeded, but this is not a functional or regression problem.

issues.description: Unconditional parenthesization rather than precedence-based check means atomic/simple expr args (e.g. a bare symbol) get redundant \left(...\right) wrapping; cosmetic only, not incorrect.

summary: Minimal, correct fix that normalizes dimensionless Function-argument dimensions to Dimension(1) so downstream dimension equality checks (e.g. in addition) recognize them as dimensionless. Preserves prior behavior for non-dimensionless args, no regression risk.

issues.description: No inline comment explaining why dimensionless dims are coerced to Dimension(1) (is_dimensionless True but object not literally Dimension(1)); a one-line comment would aid future readers.

summary: Minimal, correct fix: when locator called with renderer=None (e.g. during bbox_inches='tight' / inline backend save), it resolves renderer from ax.figure instead of the unset self.figure, avoiding the AttributeError. Matches the real root cause and is a clean two-line guard.

issues.description: No inline comment explaining why renderer can be None here (tight-bbox/print_figure path). A one-line comment would aid future maintainers, but not merge-blocking.

summary: Fix correctly changes falsy-check to explicit None-check, matching upstream Django's actual merged fix for this issue; minimal, correct, no regression risk since fields=None still behaves as before.
Fix replaces backward insert-loop with direct list concatenation, correctly preserving order of leading uncontracted gamma matrices; matches root cause described in issue and is minimal.

Correct, minimal one-line fix: `to_state.models` is keyed by the new model name, so looking it up with `old_model_name` raised KeyError when a model and field were renamed together; switching to `model_name` resolves the crash properly. `from_state` lookup correctly keeps `old_model_name`.
One-char fix corrects Morse mapping for '1' from '----' to '.----', matching standard Morse code; simple, correct, minimal.

Minimal, correct one-line fix that propagates AnnotationBbox's gid to its patch before drawing, mirroring the pattern used elsewhere in the file for other offsetbox artists. No regression or compatibility concerns.

issues.description: Only patch gid is set explicitly here; other sub-elements (e.g., arrow_patch, offsetbox) may already have their own gid handling but this PR doesn't address whether nested artists also need explicit propagation, though this matches the scope of the linked issue.

summary: Correct, minimal fix that adds current_app to the reverse() call so readonly ForeignKey links resolve against the active custom admin site, consistent with how the rest of the admin (e.g. ModelAdmin.response_add) handles namespacing. Matches the actual upstream Django resolution for this ticket.

issues.description: Trailing comma after the current_app argument would better match Django's prevailing multi-line call style, but this is a pure formatting nit and not blocking.

summary: Adds get/set_antialiased storage and accessors to Text, but the diff never wires self._antialiased into the drawing path (e.g. via the GraphicsContext), so the setter has no effect on actual rendering and the issue's core requirement is unmet.

issues.description: draw() is not updated to pass self._antialiased to the renderer/GraphicsContext (e.g. gc.set_antialiased), so set_antialiased() changes state that is never consulted during rendering — the per-artist antialiasing control the issue asks for is not actually applied.

_reset_visual_defaults (called by cla()/clear() paths) is not shown as updated to (re)initialize _antialiased, so cleared Text objects may retain a stale antialiased value inconsistent with other reset visual attributes.

summary: Minimal, targeted fix: adds `and not rep.skipped` guard so --runxfail's early-return no longer bypasses the skip-location rewriting logic below, matching the reported bug exactly. Change is a one-condition tweak that doesn't alter xfail handling in any other case.

issues.description: Comment change ('don't interfere with xfail') is fine but the branch now has two responsibilities (runxfail passthrough excluding skips) that could use a slightly clearer comment explaining why skipped reports are excluded.

summary: Correctly resolves the issue by applying the supplied `formats` to columns' `info.format` before HTML serialization, matching how other ascii writers pick up formatting. Approach is reasonable and tests pass; only minor concerns around in-place column mutation and a spurious no-op diff hunk.

issues.description: Mutates `col.info.format` on the live table columns in place. If the write path does not operate on a copy, the caller's table retains the changed format after write(), a subtle side effect. Likely acceptable/consistent with existing behavior but worth noting.
Diff includes a no-op hunk (`yield col_str` -> identical `yield col_str`), adding noise with no functional change.
No changelog/docs entry shown; a user-facing behavior fix normally warrants a changelog note (may be omitted from diff).

summary: Patch matches issue request exactly: adds allow_distinct = True to Avg and Sum, mirroring existing Count/Max/Min pattern in same file. Minimal, correct, follows existing convention.

Removes the erroneous parens from the index entry of a py:method directive using the :property: option, aligning it with how a property reads. Minimal, correct, one-line fix that resolves the reported bug.

Fix replaces strict dimension equality with equivalent_dims check for addition, correctly resolving the reported false-positive ValueError for dimensionally-equivalent addends. Minimal, targeted, uses existing DimensionSystem API.

issues.description: Returned/accumulated dimension for the sum keeps the first addend's dim rather than a canonicalized form; harmless for current usage but could surprise downstream code comparing dims strictly.

summary: Fix adds unique: False filter when deleting index_together constraints, correctly disambiguating from unique_together on same fields. Minimal, targeted, matches actual upstream Django fix for this ticket.
Correct minimal fix: adds memoryview to the isinstance check so bytes(memoryview) yields raw bytes, resolving the reported issue. Matches Django's actual accepted patch for this bug.

Moves the working `set_paths` implementation up to the base `Collection` class and drops the now-redundant `PathCollection` override, correctly enabling `ContourSet.set_paths` as requested. Minimal, correct, and idiomatic; safe to merge.

issues.description: New base-class `set_paths` (and the existing `get_paths`) lack a docstring; a one-line docstring would help the public API surface, but matching siblings already omit it so this is a nit, not blocking.

summary: Correct, minimal fix for the UnboundLocalError: it scopes `hit = kern in s` to the branch where `kern` is defined and sets `hit = False` otherwise, which is logically equivalent to the merged upstream fix and resolves the reported crash for space-free inputs. No correctness, regression, or compatibility concerns.

issues.description: Slightly cleaner alternative would be a single `hit = False` initialization before the `if` block rather than an explicit `else` branch, but the chosen form is clear and correct; purely stylistic.

summary: Correctly fixes the bug by skipping order_by expressions in GROUP BY when ordering originates from Meta.ordering (self._meta_ordering set), matching the existing logic that already strips Meta.ordering from ORDER BY. Minimal, targeted change consistent with Django conventions.

issues.description: Guard suppresses ALL order_by contributions to GROUP BY whenever _meta_ordering is set, not just the Meta.ordering-derived ones. In practice _meta_ordering being truthy means order_by was fully populated from Meta.ordering (explicit query.order_by/extra resets it), so this is safe, but it relies on that invariant rather than filtering per-expression.

summary: Core fix is correct: get_feature_names (and inverse_transform) now call _validate_vocabulary() before _check_vocabulary(), resolving the NotFittedError-when-vocabulary-provided issue consistently. However the patch also inserts a redundant duplicate of the existing 'if not hasattr(self, vocabulary_): self._validate_vocabulary()' block in transform, which is dead no-op code that a maintainer would reject.

issues.description: transform() now contains the validate-vocabulary block twice in a row; the second copy is unreachable/no-op since the first already sets vocabulary_. Obvious accidental copy-paste duplication that should be removed before merge.
The duplicated block hurts readability and signals careless editing; collapse to the single existing check.

summary: Minimal, correct fix that routes estimator-class parameters to the deepcopy/error branch by adding an `isinstance(estimator, type)` check, exactly resolving the reported `clone` failure. This is the canonical fix with no correctness, regression, or compatibility concerns.

issues.description: No inline comment explaining why `isinstance(estimator, type)` is needed (a class exposes an unbound `get_params`, so the plain `hasattr` check passes and later fails when called). A one-line comment would aid future readers, but this is a nit.

summary: The one-character `>`→`>=` change correctly fixes the mincnt>=1 inconsistency, but because the preceding `if mincnt is None: mincnt = 0` is left unchanged, the default case (mincnt unspecified, C provided) now evaluates `len(acc) >= 0`, which is always true and invokes reduce_C_function on empty bins. This regresses the documented 'at least one datum' default and breaks/changes behavior for empty cells.

issues.description: The original `len(acc) > mincnt` with `mincnt=0` (the None default) also served as an empty-bin guard. After the change, mincnt=None→0 yields `len(acc) >= 0`, which is always True, so reduce_C_function is now called on empty bins. With np.sum this draws empty cells as 0 instead of hiding them (a visible default-behavior change — and the issue's own repro uses np.sum); with np.max/np.min it raises ValueError on empty arrays; with np.mean it emits RuntimeWarnings. This is a concrete regression in the default (mincnt unspecified) C-provided path.

Fix is incomplete. It only makes mincnt>=1 consistent but mishandles the None/0 default. A correct fix must preserve the 'at least one datum' default when mincnt is None (e.g. set `mincnt = 1` for the None case, or keep an explicit non-empty guard) while using `>=` for explicit mincnt values.

Single-character flip is fragile: it conflates two distinct semantics (the empty-bin guard and the threshold comparison) that the original code combined in one `>` expression, so changing only the operator silently removes the guard for the default path.

summary: Patch buffers adjustable-file yields in a dict keyed by original name, overwriting each pass and flushing once at the end, which correctly collapses duplicate yields while still yielding non-adjustable files/exceptions immediately.

issues.description: Adjustable-file results are now only visible to callers after all passes complete rather than streamed incrementally; acceptable given generator still yields lazily, but slightly changes observable timing for consumers of collectstatic's progress output.

summary: Fix uses functools.wraps correctly so inspect.signature works, but the patch leaves the original manager_method definition in place and adds a second decorated one, producing a duplicated dead function. Functionally correct yet sloppy enough that a maintainer would push back.

issues.description: Patch does not remove the original `def manager_method` + body; it adds a second `@wraps`-decorated definition right after. Result: two consecutive identical defs where the first is dead code immediately shadowed. The clean fix should delete the old def/assignments, not duplicate the function.
Duplicated function body harms readability/maintainability — a reader sees two near-identical `manager_method` definitions with unclear intent.
`from functools import wraps` placed inside the method body rather than at module top, inconsistent with Django import conventions (functools should be a module-level import).

summary: Minimal, correct fix: wraps the partial with functools.wraps(method) so __name__/__module__/etc. are copied from the original method onto the partial, exactly resolving the AttributeError reported. This is the canonical accepted fix for Django #30961 with no regression risk.

Fix adds explicit else-raise branches so non-numeric re/im parts raise NotImplementedError instead of leaving reprec/imprec unbound, directly resolving the UnboundLocalError; matches the issue reporter's own suggested patch and is minimal and correct.

Correct, minimal fix that matches Django's actual merged solution: post_init is only connected when width_field/height_field exist, eliminating the noop signal on the hot init path. The redundant has_dimension_fields guard in update_dimension_fields is safely removable since the signal now only fires for fields that have dimension fields.

issues.description: ImageFileDescriptor.__set__ still calls update_dimension_fields(force=True) unconditionally on reassignment when previous_file is not None. With the has_dimension_fields early-return removed, an ImageField WITHOUT width/height fields now reads file.width/file.height (image I/O) and discards them on every reassignment, whereas before it returned immediately. Narrow path (reassigning an already-set value), so minor, not blocking.

summary: Fix corrects typo (undefined 'cotm' -> defined 'cothm'), resolves NameError crash exactly per issue. Minimal, correct, matches existing pattern (tanm/tanhm elsewhere in file).

Fix correctly resolves urlconf before caching, so calls with None and explicit ROOT_URLCONF hit the same cache entry, eliminating duplicate URLResolver construction. Change is minimal, targeted, and updates the one other call site (clear_url_caches) that referenced the old cache handle.

issues.description: get_resolver is no longer itself lru_cache-decorated (cache now lives on private _get_cached_resolver), so any external code calling get_resolver.cache_clear()/cache_info() directly would break. Low risk since it's an internal-ish API and the one in-tree call site was updated.
New private helper _get_cached_resolver duplicates the urlconf=None default param even though it's always called with a resolved urlconf; harmless but slightly redundant.

summary: Correct and minimal fix: SQLite's add_field now routes primary-key and unique fields (including nullable OneToOneField, which implies unique=True) through _remake_table, since ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN cannot add UNIQUE/PK columns. General, well-commented, matches existing code style.

Minimal, correct fix that removes the spurious duplicate-element check for cycle input, letting the existing Cycle composition apply non-disjoint cycles left-to-right (matching the real sympy fix). Array-form duplicate validation is preserved.

Adds symmetric reduce() methods so AddIndex/RemoveIndex pairs cancel during migration optimization, matching the issue intent. However the methods are inserted before each class docstring (demoting it to dead code) and the Remove-then-Add collapse can silently drop a differently-defined index sharing the same name.

issues.description: RemoveIndex.reduce() collapses RemoveIndex('foo') followed by AddIndex(Index(name='foo', ...)) to [], but RemoveIndex only stores the name, not the index definition. If the re-added 'foo' differs from the removed one (different fields/conditions), the optimizer cannot prove equivalence, so dropping both leaves the OLD index in place and loses the new definition — a behavioral regression in the optimizer.

reduce() is inserted as the first statement of each class body, ahead of the string literal `"""Add an index on a model."""` / `"""Remove an index from a model."""`. Since the string is no longer the first statement, it stops being the class docstring and becomes a no-op expression. Method should be placed after the docstring.
The single-line isinstance condition far exceeds Django's enforced line length (black/flake8, 88 cols) and would fail the project's lint/CI style checks; condition should be wrapped.

summary: Fix correctly prevents the handler variable from being overwritten when MiddlewareNotUsed is raised, using a temporary adapted_handler and committing it only via the try/else clause on success. This is a minimal, targeted fix matching the root cause described in the issue.

issues.description: Relies on try/except/else control flow which is correct but slightly less obvious at a glance than an explicit conditional; a brief comment could clarify why the assignment is deferred to the else branch.

summary: Fix directly matches the root cause described in the issue: bulk_update()'s isinstance(attr, Expression) check missed plain F() objects, which don't subclass Expression, causing str(F()) to be stored as CASE value instead of resolving the referenced column. The minimal one-line widening of the isinstance check to include F is exactly one of the two fixes the reporter suggested and is what upstream Django actually merged.

issues.description: isinstance(attr, (Expression, F)) is a narrower fix than duck-typing on hasattr(attr, 'resolve_expression'); any future non-Expression, non-F class implementing resolve_expression would hit the same bug. Not blocking since F is the only such case in current Django and matches the issue's proposed fix.

summary: Adding `dtype=[np.float64, np.float32]` to `check_X_y` makes `HuberRegressor.fit` coerce boolean (and other) inputs to float, fixing the `TypeError` in `_huber_loss_and_gradient` exactly as `LinearRegression` already does. Minimal, correct, convention-aligned fix.
Patch correctly saves and restores the handler level, fixing the caplog level leak between tests. Minimal, targeted, matches the existing restore pattern for logger levels.

issues.description: set_level saves handler level with plain assignment (not setdefault like logger levels), so repeated set_level calls overwrite _initial_handler_level with an already-modified level. But since handler.level starts at 0 and both saves capture pre-mutation state correctly on first call, and subsequent calls capture the prior set level — restoration to true original only guaranteed on first call. Edge case, unlikely to matter in practice; logger levels use setdefault for exactly this reason.

summary: Minimal one-line fix passes `using=db` explicitly to `save()` so the content type update runs on the correct database connection instead of silently falling back to the router/default, matching Django's standard `Model.save(using=...)` idiom.

The patch correctly adds the field name to the readonly_fields check error message, unifying it with other checks (list_editable, etc.) as the issue requested. Placeholder count (4 %s) matches the argument tuple, the change is minimal and idiomatic, and it resolves the issue cleanly.
Correctly handles the 1-element tuple special case by emitting a trailing comma, matching Python's tuple repr. Minimal, targeted, no regression to multi-element or empty tuples.

issues.description: The explicit if/else could be folded into a single comprehension+join with a conditional trailing comma, but the current form is clear and readable; pure nit.

summary: One-line regex fix restricts user:pass authentication segment to exclude unencoded ':', '@', '/' per RFC 1738, correctly rejecting URLs like http://foo/bar@example.com. Minimal, correct, matches Django's actual merged fix for this issue.

One-character typo fix correcting an undefined-name reference (`cotm` → `cothm`) in `coth.eval`, where `cothm` was already bound on the preceding line. Resolves the reported `NameError` exactly and is minimal and correct.

Removes a buggy short-circuit that returned the input unchanged when it was already in NFKD form, so accents are now stripped from pre-normalized strings as the issue requires. Correct, minimal, no regression.

issues.description: Drops the early-return fast path for strings with no combining characters, so every input now allocates a new joined string via the list comprehension. Negligible cost and the old fast path was the source of the bug, so not worth retaining.

summary: Minimal, correct change that implements exactly what the issue requested: assume real_apps is a set (internal API) and assert it rather than coercing. Behavior is equivalent for all valid inputs, including empty sets.

issues.description: Uses assert for argument validation, which is stripped under python -O. Acceptable here since this is documented internal API and matches the issue's explicit request, but a maintainer could prefer a raised exception.

summary: Fix replaces the incorrect all-ones fill for the right-hand block with the actual separability values from `right`, correctly propagating non-trivial separability into the combined coordinate matrix for nested CompoundModels. This is the same minimal, targeted fix as the accepted upstream astropy patch for this issue.

Correct, minimal fix that short-circuits ModelBackend.authenticate() when username or password is None, avoiding a useless DB query and needless password hasher run. Matches the issue's recommendation and Django conventions; no correctness or compatibility problems.

issues.description: Behavior changes when password is None but username is valid: previously it ran the timing-mask hasher; now returns None early. Outcome is equivalent (auth still fails) and the timing-mask is intentionally dropped per the issue rationale, so no real regression.

summary: Minimal, correct fix that rejects URLs containing forbidden whitespace characters (CR/LF/tab) before any parsing, closing the gap created by CPython's bpo-43882 splitting change. Matches the maintainers' actual accepted approach and introduces no regression or compatibility issue.

issues.description: unsafe_chars check placed before scheme validation; a short comment explaining why (CPython strips these chars during urlsplit) would help future readers but isn't required.

summary: Minimal, idiomatic fix replacing truthiness test of `im(a)` with fuzzy `im(a).is_zero is False`, correctly preventing the false-positive ValueError when `im` stays unevaluated under `evaluate(False)` while still rejecting genuinely imaginary coordinates. Aligns with SymPy's standard three-valued assumption idiom and is the correct, mergeable resolution.

issues.description: Semantics shift on the unknown case: when `im(a).is_zero` returns None (indeterminate) for a number, the old code raised but the new code permits the coordinate. For actual numbers (`is_number` guard) the imaginary part is normally decidable, so this is a corner case, but it slightly relaxes the rejection to only definitely-imaginary values.

summary: One-line default change of SECURE_REFERRER_POLICY from None to 'same-origin' correctly implements the issue's security hardening; SecurityMiddleware already reads this setting so the header takes effect with no further code needed. This is a deliberate, documented secure-default change appropriate for a major release.

issues.description: Changing the default sends Referrer-Policy: same-origin on all responses, which can break third-party sites relying on the Referer header for verification. This is a known, accepted backward-compat tradeoff noted in the issue and warrants a release-notes/backwards-incompatible-changes entry (docs not shown in diff).

Such a security default change normally needs accompanying documentation updates (settings.txt default value, security release notes). Not shown in the source-only diff, so likely handled separately, but worth confirming before merge.

summary: Minimal, correct fix: yields ms.copy() instead of shared dict, removes now-obsolete docstring caveat/doctests. Matches issue request directly with no scope creep.

issues.description: Adds a dict copy per yielded partition; acceptable and expected trade-off per the issue's own reasoning, negligible for typical partition sizes.

summary: Fix narrowly and correctly implements the issue's proposed check, replacing an overly broad __file__ test with a combined __file__/__path__ check consistent with Python's documented namespace-package semantics. Minimal, low-risk, single-line change with no apparent regression for normal (non-frozen) environments.

issues.description: isinstance(module.__path__, list) checks for exact type rather than duck-typing/ABC, so a non-namespace importer that supplies a list-subclass or list-like __path__ could still be misclassified; acceptable given CPython's actual namespace implementation but slightly implementation-detail-coupled, as the issue itself acknowledges.

summary: Patch special-cases extension containing I to bypass _generic_factor and call a different factor implementation entirely, rather than fixing root cause in the domain/extension handling; doesn't address extension=True or other algebraic extensions per issue title.

issues.description: Hack special-cases 'I in extension list' and routes to sympy.simplify.simplify.factor instead of fixing _generic_factor's handling of extensions; wrong abstraction, brittle condition on exact extension contents.
Issue title says 'extension=True' drops factor; patch only handles extension as list containing I, so extension=True or extension=[sqrt(2)] etc. still broken/untouched.
Fix narrowly targets exact reported case (extension=[I]) rather than general bug in multivariate factor+extension path, likely overfit to reproduction test.

Routing through sympy.simplify.simplify.factor for any extension containing I changes behavior/semantics (different algorithm, possible domain mismatch) for all such calls, unverified against broader extension use cases.

summary: Minimal correct fix: Contains(x, S).as_set() returning S matches the intended semantics (x ranges over S) and resolves the AttributeError in Piecewise/relational code paths without altering other behavior.

issues.description: Assumes args[0] is the free symbol being solved for; for Contains(expr, S) with a non-trivial expr (e.g. Contains(x+1, Reals)) as_set() silently returns S rather than the true solution set, whereas previously it raised NotImplementedError. Silent-wrong is slightly worse than explicit-unimplemented for that edge case, but this matches the common usage pattern (Piecewise cond.as_set()) and is a reasonable minimal fix.

summary: Patch correctly fixes the precision loss by passing through native Decimal inputs untouched instead of round-tripping them through float; non-Decimal paths are unchanged, so no regression. Minimal, targeted, and mergeable.

issues.description: Special Decimal values (NaN, Infinity) now bypass the previous float-normalization path (which turned them into Decimal('nan')/etc.) and reach the formatting logic as the original Decimal object. Downstream as_tuple()/quantize handling appears robust, but this is a subtle behavior shift worth a regression test; not merge-blocking.
The nested try/except inside the else branch is a bit dense; a maintainer might prefer flattening, but it preserves the exact original fallback semantics so readability is acceptable.

summary: Diff systematically routes subexpression formatting through self._print instead of str()/direct interpolation, correctly making StrPrinter settings (e.g. sympy_integers) propagate into Eq, Limit, Lambda, Permutation, etc. Change is minimal, confined to str.py, and directly targets the reported bug without altering unrelated behavior (unhandled types still fall back to str() via emptyPrinter, so no regression for non-sympifiable attributes like domain/order).

issues.description: Minor readability/style inconsistency in continuation-line indentation and use of tuple(map(self._print, (...))) in _print_Limit vs explicit self._print() calls used elsewhere in the same diff.

summary: Adds a `__str__` returning `str(self.value)` to the `Choices` base, correctly fixing the enum-value type mismatch so all subclasses (Text/IntegerChoices) print their value instead of `MyEnum.MEMBER`. This matches the actual upstream Django fix and is minimal and correct.

issues.description: Inserted blank line after the docstring contains trailing whitespace, which would trip flake8/isort-style checks; cosmetic only.

summary: Correct, minimal fix that passes the already-computed self.prog_name to CommandParser so usage/error output and prog reflect the parsed argv instead of sys.argv[0]. Matches the issue's suggested patch and follows existing code conventions; mergeable.

Correct, minimal fix that resolves the `-> None` return annotation crash by skipping the unit conversion when the annotation is None, matching the issue's suggested approach. Matches the fix astropy actually merged.

issues.description: Uses `not in (..., None)` which relies on `==` equality rather than `is None` identity; harmless here since unit/empty objects compare cleanly against None, but `is` would be slightly more idiomatic for sentinel checks.

summary: Fix adds early-return guard in collect_pages so epub builds skip module-page generation when viewcode_enable_epub=False, directly resolving reported bug with minimal, targeted change consistent with existing should_generate_module_page pattern.

issues.description: Trailing diff hunk on the setup() return dict shows only a newline-at-EOF change, unrelated noise but harmless.

summary: Core fix is correct: passing multi_class=multi_class makes the scoring instance use the same multinomial/ovr probability computation as LogisticRegressionCV, resolving the reported neg_log_loss discrepancy. However the diff also drops the pre-existing fit_intercept=fit_intercept argument, an unnecessary deviation from the issue's suggested fix that a maintainer would ask to restore.

issues.description: The patch replaces `LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=fit_intercept)` with `LogisticRegression(multi_class=multi_class)`, removing the previously-passed fit_intercept argument rather than adding multi_class alongside it (the issue suggested `LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=fit_intercept, multi_class=multi_class)`). In current code this is functionally harmless because the instance's coef_/intercept_ are set manually and .fit() is never called on it, so fit_intercept is unused at predict/score time and tests still pass. But silently dropping a constructor arg is a confusing, regression-prone de
Minimal-correct fix would keep both arguments; omitting fit_intercept makes the intent less clear to future readers who may assume fit_intercept genuinely doesn't matter here.

summary: Correctly converts the scaled float min_samples to an int via int(round(...)), resolving the TypeError raised by NearestNeighbors while preserving the existing max(2, ...) lower bound. Minimal, targeted fix that matches the bug report exactly.

issues.description: Inline comment explaining the int(round(...)) Python2/3 rounding-semantics rationale (given in the PR description) is not carried into the code, leaving the intent slightly implicit for future readers.

summary: Correct, minimal fix replacing `^...$` with `\A...\Z` in both username validators, which properly rejects trailing-newline usernames — this matches Django's actual upstream resolution. Only trivial diff noise (a stray leading blank line and a no-op `flags = 0` re-write) detracts.

issues.description: Adds a stray blank line at the top of the file before `import re`, unrelated to the fix. Should be dropped to keep the diff clean.
`flags = 0` is shown as removed and re-added with no semantic change (whitespace/newline noise), adding pointless churn to the diff.

summary: Minimal one-character fix changing `p < 0` to `p <= 0` so the integer-shortcut branch handles arg=0 with no fractional remainder, avoiding the `prec` ValueError on inputs like '0.00'. Correct, targeted, and consistent with how floatformat already handles the no-mantissa case.

issues.description: No inline comment explaining why the boundary became <= 0 (covers arg==0 with zero remainder), but the surrounding code is similarly terse, so not required.

summary: Minimal, correct fix that restores 3.6.0 behavior for all-nan bar data by catching StopIteration from _safe_first_finite and falling back to safe_first_element; matches upstream resolution and handles both x0 and xconv symmetrically.

issues.description: Relies on StopIteration leaking out of cbook._safe_first_finite as the signal for 'no finite element', which is a slightly implicit contract between the two helpers; the explanatory comments mitigate this and it mirrors the existing exception-handling pattern, so not blocking.

summary: Correct, minimal one-line fix: '%04d' format zero-pads years < 1000 to four digits, matching the documented 'Year, 4 digits' contract. No regression for years >= 1000 (min-width formatting leaves them unchanged).

Fix correctly changes show_save_as_new to check has_add_permission instead of has_change_permission, since save-as-new creates a new object and should be gated on add rights, not change rights. Matches the actual upstream Django fix for this ticket.

The patch fixes the reported `.Z`/`.br` cases but does so with fragile `filename.endswith()` string matching instead of extending the adjacent encoding map dict that already holds the analogous gzip/bzip2/xz entries. Functionally correct for the report, but a Django maintainer would reject this approach in favor of the trivial idiomatic fix.

issues.description: The `mimetypes.guess_type` call already yields an `encoding` ('compress' for .Z, 'br' for .br). The correct, idiomatic fix is to add `"br": "application/x-brotli", "compress": "application/x-compress"` to the existing encoding->content_type dict immediately above. Re-deriving the extension via `filename.endswith()` ignores the value mimetypes already computed and is the wrong abstraction; a maintainer would request the encoding-map approach.

Special-casing two literal suffixes (`.Z`, `.br`) does not generalize and bypasses the encoding-handling mechanism. Future encodings would need yet more endswith branches rather than one dict entry, and the suffix check is case-sensitive (won't match e.g. `.BR`), unlike the mimetypes encoding detection.
Uses single-quoted string literals ('.Z', '.br') while Django is black-formatted with double quotes throughout; this would be reflowed/flagged by Django's enforced black/style checks.
Adds an if/elif/else that duplicates content-type resolution logic right after the encoding map is built, making the block harder to read than a single dict-based assignment.

summary: Correct and minimal fix for the RenameModel-with-fixed-db_table noop bug; when old and new db_table match, the operation short-circuits before touching the main table, related-object FKs, and M2M tables, all of which key off db_table and thus need no change. Matches Django's actual accepted fix.

issues.description: Comment 'Don't alter when a table name is not changed.' is slightly terse; could note that related FK/M2M alterations are also intentionally skipped since they derive from db_table. Non-blocking.

summary: Moves the `sys.exit(1)` for `--check` before the migration-writing step so `makemigrations --check` exits without writing files, matching `migrate --check`/`optimizemigration --check` and the issue's request. Minimal, correct, help text updated.

issues.description: Help-text wording 'and don't actually write them' is slightly awkward and could read cleaner, but conveys the new behavior. Stylistic nit only.

summary: Minimal, correct fix: guards the deprecation warning and the categorical-units info log behind a non-empty size check, so empty arrays (where `all(...)` vacuously returns True) no longer trigger a spurious MatplotlibDeprecationWarning/ConversionError. Both `values` and `data` are numpy arrays in these methods, so `.size` is safe.

issues.description: No inline comment explaining that the `.size` guard exists to suppress the vacuous-true `all()` result on empty input; future readers may not see why the check was added.

summary: Code change is correct, minimal, and resolves the issue by threading fill_value through to the initial SimpleImputer. However it adds a public parameter with no docstring entry or versionadded directive, which scikit-learn requires (and numpydoc validation enforces) before merge.

issues.description: New public parameter `fill_value` is added to the signature and `_parameter_constraints` but is not documented in the class docstring, and lacks the required `.. versionadded::` directive. scikit-learn mandates docstring coverage for all public params (checked by numpydoc/test_docstring_parameters); maintainers will not merge an undocumented public parameter.

Constraint `[object]` disables real validation (mirrors SimpleImputer, so acceptable), but a brief check that np.nan is intended/supported as fill_value—explicitly requested in the issue for tree estimators—would strengthen confidence; not a code defect on its own.

summary: One-line fix correctly distinguishes an undefined `__all__` (None) from an empty `__all__` ([]), so an empty `__all__` now suppresses all members as expected. Minimal, correct, and consistent with how `self.__all__` is initialized to None.

Correct, minimal fix that replaces the `in` membership test (which triggers `__eq__` and the numpy array truth-ambiguity ValueError) with identity checks against each sentinel. Sentinels (mock.DEFAULT) are singletons, so `is` comparison is semantically correct and resolves the bug generally.

issues.description: Multi-line list-comprehension reformatting is a slight style choice; a single inline `any(...)` generator would keep the diff tighter, but this is cosmetic and does not affect correctness.

summary: Adds `__hash__` to ModelChoiceIteratorValue, correctly restoring hashability that was lost when `__eq__` was defined without a matching `__hash__` (Python sets `__hash__` to None). The implementation is consistent with `__eq__` (both delegate to `self.value`) and matches the canonical upstream fix.

Small, correct change enforcing the documented internal-API contract that real_apps is always a set, replacing defensive conversion with an assertion per the issue's request. Cleanly resolves the linked issue with no regression or compatibility concern.

Correct, minimal fix: replaces the hardcoded get_current_timezone_name() with self.get_tzname() from the TimeZone mixin, so a passed tzinfo is honored while preserving USE_TZ=False (returns None) behavior. Resolves the issue exactly as reported with no regression risk.

The patch silences the warning by calling self._check_feature_names(X, reset=True) on the internally-validated ndarray, which has the side effect of deleting the fitted feature_names_in_ attribute. This trades the spurious warning for a real regression in fitted-estimator state.

issues.description: By the offset_ computation step X is the validated ndarray (no feature names). _check_feature_names(X, reset=True) on an input without feature names does not just 'validate' — it delattr's feature_names_in_. The warning disappears only because the attribute is destroyed, so the subsequent reset=False check inside score_samples finds nothing to compare. This is a hacky fix exploiting a destructive side effect rather than suppressing the warning correctly (e.g. a private _score_samples that skips re-validation, or warnings.catch_warnings).

Concrete regression: after fitting IsolationForest on a DataFrame with contamination != 'auto', clf.feature_names_in_ is deleted and no longer exists, violating the estimator contract. Existing common tests (check_dataframe_column_names_consistency) use default contamination='auto', which hits the early-return branch before this line, so they never exercise the path — that's why the suite still passes despite the broken behavior.
Comment 'Validate feature names before calling score_samples' mischaracterizes the call — its actual operative effect here is resetting/removing feature_names_in_, not validation.

summary: Fix suppresses spurious rtype field for classes when __init__ return annotation is None; minimal targeted change matching issue, no regression apparent for non-class or non-None-returning cases.

issues.description: Suppression keyed on string equality annotation == 'None' rather than checking actual return type value; fragile but consistent with existing string-based annotation handling in this module.

summary: Reverts Field.__hash__ to depend only on the immutable creation_counter, fixing the hash-mutability bug exactly as the reporter suggested. Correct, minimal, and safe since equality was already fixed in #31750.

Minimal, correct fix that makes renderer optional in AnchoredLocatorBase.__call__ and resolves it from ax.figure when None, exactly matching the traceback's failure path during tight-bbox save. Resolves the issue without regression or compatibility concerns.

issues.description: Relies on private API ax.figure._get_renderer(); acceptable since this is internal mpl_toolkits code already coupled to such internals, but ties the locator to that private method.

summary: Minimal, idiomatic one-line fix: `max(..., default=None)` returns None for empty item sets instead of raising ValueError, which is cleaner than the issue's suggested broad `except (TypeError, ValueError)`. Correctly resolves the bug without affecting non-empty cases or the existing TypeError guard.

Correct, minimal noop guard equivalent to the accepted Django fix: when old and new db_table match, database_forwards returns early (and database_backwards delegates to it, so both directions are covered). No correctness or regression concerns; only minor readability/comment nits.

issues.description: Condition inlines `from_state.apps.get_model(app_label, self.old_name)._meta.db_table` rather than binding `old_db_table`/`new_db_table` locals; long expression is harder to read and the old_model lookup is duplicated with the line below the guard.
No comment explaining why the early return is a noop (e.g. 'Don't alter when the table name is unchanged'); a one-line comment would clarify intent for future maintainers.
Guard placed before the `allow_migrate_model` check instead of inside it as in the surrounding pattern; outcome is identical (noop in all combinations) but placement differs slightly from repo idiom.

summary: Correctly bumps the SQLite minimum version check from 3.8.3 to 3.9.0 and updates the error message to match, fully resolving the issue with a minimal, targeted change. No correctness, regression, or compatibility problems in the source change.

issues.description: Supported-databases documentation (docs/ref/databases.txt) and release notes would normally be updated alongside a minimum-version bump; not shown in this diff. Non-blocking and typically handled in the same PR's doc files.

summary: Adding .distinct() after complex_filter() is the standard, minimal fix for duplicate rows caused by join-based limit_choices_to Q filters, and mirrors Django's actual accepted fix for this issue.

issues.description: distinct() adds a DISTINCT clause which can be marginally slower on large querysets, but this is the correct tradeoff to eliminate join-induced duplicates.

summary: Minimal, correct fix replacing `del deconstruction[2]['to']` with `deconstruction[2].pop('to', None)`, exactly resolving the KeyError when a custom FK field hardcodes and removes its `to` kwarg. Behavior is unchanged when `to` is present; idiomatic and merge-ready.

Correctly exposes the existing skip_checks stealth option as a real --skip-checks CLI flag, gated on requires_system_checks, matching Django's actual merged fix for this ticket. No blocking problems; a few minor compatibility/robustness nits worth noting.

issues.description: Removing 'skip_checks' from base_stealth_options means call_command('cmd', skip_checks=True) on a command with requires_system_checks=False now raises TypeError (unknown option) instead of silently accepting it as before. The flag is a no-op for such commands anyway, so impact is small, but it is a subtle behavioral change for programmatic callers.

options['skip_checks'] (subscript) is slightly more fragile than the prior options.get('skip_checks'); it relies on short-circuit evaluation of self.requires_system_checks plus the parser always supplying the store_true default. A direct execute(**options) call with requires_system_checks=True but no skip_checks key would KeyError. Safe for all standard parser/call_command paths.
A new user-facing CLI option ideally warrants docs/ref/django-admin.txt and release-note updates; not present in the shown source diff (may be omitted like tests).

summary: Minimal, correct fix that guards MaxLengthValidator append on a non-None max_length, matching the existing BinaryField.__init__ precedent and avoiding an extraneous, broken validator on output-field CharField() instances. Resolves the reported issue with no apparent correctness, regression, or compatibility risk.

Clean, well-scoped feature that wires a per-Text antialiased state through the GraphicsContext into the agg and cairo backends; mirrors existing artist get/set_antialiased conventions and resolves the issue. The math-text limitation is documented and only minor API/consistency nits remain, so it is mergeable.

issues.description: Per-Text antialiased setting has no effect on math expressions (mathtext follows a separate draw path). This is a real functional gap but it is explicitly documented in the set_antialiased docstring, so it is an acceptable known limitation rather than a blocker.

Cairo's new GraphicsContext.get_antialiased() returns a cairo ANTIALIAS_* enum, whereas the base GraphicsContextBase.get_antialiased() returns a bool. It is self-consistent within the cairo backend (fed straight into set_antialias/set_font_options), but it diverges from the base-class return contract; harmless here since no cross-backend code depends on it.

set_antialiased docstring wording is slightly confusing ('Antialiasing will be determined by rc:text.antialiased and the parameter will have no effect if the text contains math') — could more clearly state the math-only caveat. Cosmetic.

summary: Mathematically identical refactor (sqrt(tk/pk)*sqrt(tk/qk) == tk/sqrt(pk*qk) for tk>0) that computes float divisions before the sqrt, avoiding the int overflow in pk*qk. Correct, minimal, and resolves the reported RuntimeWarning/nan.

issues.description: No inline comment explaining why the algebraically-equivalent split form is used (overflow avoidance); a one-line note would aid future readers, but not required by repo convention.

summary: Fix correctly addresses fcntl.flock() return-value bug by catching exceptions instead of checking a return code; using BlockingIOError specifically (rather than broad OSError as in the original issue suggestion) is actually more correct since it only swallows the expected non-blocking-lock-failure case while letting other OS errors propagate.
