Minimal, correct fix: adds `isinstance(estimator, type)` so class objects (which have an unbound `get_params`) route to the deepcopy/error branch instead of calling `get_params()` without `self`. This is the canonical upstream fix; general (covers any estimator-type param, not just the reported one) and low-risk.

issues.description: No inline comment explaining why the `isinstance(estimator, type)` guard is needed (classes expose an unbound get_params). Optional, non-blocking.

summary: The patch stops the crash for the trivial ascending-F case but is the wrong fix: it coerces an OrderBy into `field.expression.name`, discarding the OrderBy's direction and expression semantics, and breaks on expressions without a `.name`. The proper fix preserves the OrderBy object in `find_ordering_name` rather than flattening it to a string in `get_order_dir`.

issues.description: Fix is at the wrong layer and loses information. `get_order_dir` is forced to return a plain field name + default direction, so an OrderBy like `F('x').desc()` is reduced to ('x', 'ASC') — the descending flag and any non-trivial expression behavior are silently dropped. The correct approach (the one Django merged) intercepts the item in `find_ordering_name`/`get_order_by` and keeps it as an OrderBy object instead of stringifying it.

Incomplete: `field.expression.name` assumes the wrapped expression has a `.name` attribute. For `Meta.ordering` entries such as `Lower('name').asc()`, `Coalesce(...)`, or any Func/Combined expression, `.expression` has no `.name`, so this raises AttributeError — a new crash for the broader class of the very bug being fixed.

Passes only because the reproduction case uses an ascending F-expression, where coercing to the bare field name happens to yield equivalent SQL. The change is special-cased to that scenario rather than being a general resolution of expression ordering.

`hasattr(field, 'expression')` is loose duck-typing; Django idiom here would use `isinstance(field, OrderBy)` (or check `resolve_expression`) and would not reuse the low-level `get_order_dir` string helper for this purpose.

summary: Wraps the formset prefix in re.escape() before building the pk regex, correctly fixing the data-loss/regex-injection bug for prefixes containing special characters. Minimal, targeted, and the pk.name argument is safe since model field names follow Python identifier rules.

Two-line fix wires HTML writer into the same `_set_col_formats`/`self.data.cols` mechanism already used by other ASCII writers, correctly resolving the reported formats-ignored bug via the existing infrastructure rather than a one-off hack.
Minimal one-line fix correctly distinguishes fields=None (no filtering) from fields=[] (filter everything out), resolving the reported bug without altering other behavior.

Correct, minimal fix to `_cstack`: replacing the hardcoded `= 1` assignment with `= right` preserves the nested submodel's separability structure instead of flattening it to all-True, which is exactly what caused non-separable results for nested CompoundModels. This is the right general fix, not a test-specific hack.

issues.description: No inline comment added explaining why the right block is copied verbatim (right.shape[0] vs right.shape[1] asymmetry); a one-line note would aid future maintainers, but not merge-blocking.

summary: The np.where rewrite correctly eliminates the NumPy 1.24 out-of-bound-integer deprecation warnings by building a new, type-promoted array instead of forcing 256/257/258 into a uint8 array in place, while preserving the over-before-under ordering and even fixing a latent uint8 wraparound. Mergeable; only a modest memory/perf consideration is worth noting.

issues.description: np.where allocates three new full-size arrays and rewrites every element each call, whereas the original in-place fancy-index assignment only touched the (usually few) out-of-range/bad entries. On large image arrays in this hot colormap path this adds avoidable allocation/copy overhead, though it is acceptable and not blocking.

For integer (e.g. uint8) input, xa is now widened to a larger int dtype via type promotion instead of staying uint8. Downstream uses xa only as an index into self._lut (lut.take/indexing), which is dtype-agnostic, so this is harmless and arguably more correct (avoids the old 257->1 wraparound), but it is a behavior change worth being aware of.

summary: Adds 'has_add_permission' check to 'show_save_as_new', correctly preventing the 'save as new' button (which creates a new object) from appearing for users lacking add permission. Minimal, correct, and exactly matches the issue.

Clean, minimal change that adds `fill_value` to IterativeImputer by mirroring the existing SimpleImputer parameter and delegating validation to the internal SimpleImputer. Correctly resolves the issue (including np.nan support via the `no_validation` constraint) with proper docstring and signature placement next to `initial_strategy`.

issues.description: `.. versionadded:: 1.3` is hard-coded; should be confirmed to match the actual release branch, but this is a trivial maintainer-adjustable detail.

summary: Adding `__str__` returning `str(self.value)` on the base `Choices` class is the canonical, minimal fix for the type-display mismatch and matches Django's actual merged solution. No correctness, regression, or compatibility concerns.

issues.description: Overriding `__str__` changes str() output for all Choices members (e.g. logging/repr-adjacent display now shows 'first' instead of 'MyChoice.FIRST_CHOICE'); intended and desirable here, but a behavioral shift worth noting. Not blocking.

summary: Correct, minimal fix: the leading uncontracted gamma matrices were inserted at position 0 in forward order, which reverses them; iterating the index range backward restores correct order. Matches the issue's root-cause analysis and resolves both reported cases.

issues.description: Second diff hunk on `return t` is a no-op (only adds a trailing newline at end of file); harmless but unrelated to the fix.

summary: Adds _print_Min and _print_Max to PythonCodePrinter mapping to Python builtins min/max, exactly matching the issue's suggested fix. Correct, minimal, follows existing printer-method convention.
Correct, minimal fix that restores pre-3.0 behavior by forcing INSERT only when pk has a default AND no explicit pk was set; matches the issue's suggested resolution and Django's actual merged patch.
Patch correctly fixes the bug: passed symbols are now honored when count matches, and ring.symbols is used only when no symbols are given. Minimal, correct, no regression risk.

issues.description: The nested `else: if not symbols:` could be expressed more cleanly as an `elif not symbols:` on the original `if`, but the logic is correct and readable as-is.

summary: Minimal one-line fix resolves the UnboundLocalError by ensuring 'kern' is always bound before the later unconditional 'hit = kern in s' check; using '' as the default is a bit incidental (it makes hit truthy even when no space-kerning occurred) but since Symbol('') never appears in the parsed expression the subsequent subs is a no-op, so no observed behavioral regression.

issues.description: kern = '' as a sentinel makes 'hit = kern in s' trivially True whenever no space substitution happened, which is semantically odd (relies on Symbol('') not appearing in the sympified expression) rather than being an explicit, self-documenting guard like tracking hit separately.

summary: Minimal, correct fix that short-circuits ModelBackend.authenticate() when username or password is None, avoiding a useless DB query and needless password hashing for credentials meant for another backend. Matches the issue's recommended solution with no correctness, regression, or compatibility concerns.

issues.description: Could add a short comment explaining why the early return is safe (credentials intended for another backend; timing-masking concern does not extend across backends), mirroring the existing explanatory comment style in this method. Non-blocking.

summary: Fix replace hacky _find_pivot with _find_reasonable_pivot + expand_mul zero test, correctly resolve NaN comparison bug in Bareiss algorithm for symbolic matrices. random_complex_number tolerance param support internal numeric zero-testing, not scope creep.

issues.description: randtest.py change touch unrelated-looking file, but tolerance param needed by _find_reasonable_pivot's randomized zero test, so related not creep.
_is_zero_after_expand_mul docstring terse, could clarify why expand_mul chosen over full simplify (perf tradeoff noted in code comment though).

summary: One-line fix assigns the discarded `cancel(ret)` result back to `ret`, so the Bareiss fraction actually gets cancelled/simplified instead of accumulating into an expression that eventually collapses to nan and crashes. Minimal, correct, targets root cause.

Correct, minimal fix that extends call_command's kwargs-to-parse_args logic to include options belonging to a required mutually exclusive group, directly resolving the reported issue. Matches existing file conventions and introduces no regression.

issues.description: Relies on argparse private attributes (_mutually_exclusive_groups, _group_actions). This is consistent with the surrounding code which already uses parser._actions, so acceptable, but it is coupling to undocumented internals.

summary: Correctly rewrites _check_list_display_item to try get_field then getattr, returning E108 only when both fail, matching the issue's recommended fix and resolving the false E108 on instance-only descriptor fields like PositionField. Minimal, general, and consistent with existing E108/E109 semantics — this is essentially the canonical upstream fix.

issues.description: The `field` variable is assigned across two try/except branches before the isinstance check; while every path reaching the check is guaranteed to bind it, a brief comment would make the control flow easier to follow for future readers.

summary: Minimal, correct fix matching issue: sets allow_distinct=True on Avg and Sum consistent with existing Count/Max/Min pattern. No regression or compatibility risk.

Correct, minimal one-line fix that adds the missing get_swappable_settings_name.cache_clear() call to clear_cache(), exactly matching the documented contract that all internal caches be cleared. get_swappable_settings_name is an lru_cache-wrapped method and clearing it on registry changes is correct with no regression risk.

Minimal, correct fix: replacing the hand-rolled AttributeError with a re-call to self.__getattribute__(attr) lets a nested AttributeError (e.g. from a subclass property accessing a missing attribute) propagate with the correct attribute name, while the normal missing-attribute path still produces the standard Python message. This is the well-known idiom and introduces no recursion or message-format regression.

issues.description: On the error path __getattribute__ re-runs full attribute lookup, so any property getter is invoked a second time; side-effecting getters would execute twice. Only affects the failure path, negligible in practice.

Comment 'this will give correct exception' is terse; a brief note explaining that an explicit __getattribute__ call does not re-trigger __getattr__ (hence no recursion) and surfaces the original nested AttributeError would aid future maintainers.

summary: Patch correctly appends QUERY_STRING to the APPEND_SLASH redirect, fully resolving the dropped-query-string bug with proper empty-query handling. Functionally correct; only idiom/style nits, no blocking problems.

issues.description: Django/Black house style uses double quotes; patch uses single quotes for 'QUERY_STRING' and ''. Inconsistent with surrounding code ("%s/" % request.path).

Reinvents existing helper. request.get_full_path(force_append_slash=True) yields path+slash+query in one call, matching CommonMiddleware's idiom; the manual string-build with if/else is more verbose but behaviorally equivalent.

summary: Minimal, correct fix that passes the pivot's tzinfo (and explicit microsecond=0) into the datetime constructor, resolving the offset-naive vs offset-aware subtraction TypeError when USE_TZ=True. Matches the issue author's proposed solution and introduces no regression for naive datetimes (tzinfo=None preserves prior behavior).

One-line change makes Contains.as_set return the containing set (args[1]) instead of raising NotImplementedError, correctly resolving the Piecewise AttributeError since the set of values satisfying x ∈ S is S itself. Minimal, correct for the reported case, and consistent with as_set semantics.

issues.description: Returns args[1] unconditionally, so for a non-trivial element expression (e.g. Contains(x+1, S)) the result is not the true solution set of the free symbol but the raw set S. Acceptable for the typical symbol-membership case and matches sympy's loose as_set usage, but not a fully general solution.
No docstring/comment added explaining why as_set returns the containing set; a brief note would aid future maintainers.

summary: One-line fix adds `cls._clear_cached_lookups()` to `_unregister_lookup`, exactly mirroring the existing call in `register_lookup`. Correct, minimal, and idiomatic resolution of the stale-cache bug.

Minimal fix mirrors existing pattern used in transform() (call _validate_vocabulary() before checking), correctly resolves the inconsistency described in the issue without altering behavior for the unfitted-no-vocabulary case.

Patch correctly restores the missing maxlength HTML attribute on AuthenticationForm's username field by setting widget.attrs['maxlength'] alongside the field's max_length, directly fixing the #27515 regression. Minimal, targeted, no regression or compatibility risk.

Removes a blind string replace that corrupted parametrize IDs containing '.[' as literal characters; the fix is minimal, targets the actual root cause in getmodpath, and doesn't special-case only the reported input.

issues.description: Author admits uncertainty about why the original .replace('.[', '[') hack existed; no comment explains the historical purpose being removed, but full test suite passing mitigates regression risk.

summary: Adds a natural __iter__ to Paginator that yields pages over page_range, exactly matching the issue request. Correct, minimal, idiomatic; no regression or compatibility concern since Paginator had no prior __iter__.

The patch correctly fixes the misleading AttributeError: when a class-level descriptor (e.g. a property) raises AttributeError internally, it now re-dispatches via object.__getattribute__ so the real underlying error surfaces instead of masking it as 'prop' missing. Logic is correct, minimal, and recursion-safe since object.__getattribute__ does not re-trigger __getattr__.

issues.description: The new branch relies on the subtle fact that object.__getattribute__ (unlike the type-level lookup hook) does not fall back to __getattr__, so a descriptor's internal AttributeError propagates instead of recursing. A short comment explaining this intent would aid future maintainers.

The original '# Fail' comment now sits inside the if-branch and the success path (return object.__getattribute__) is uncommented; a one-line note on why re-dispatch is needed would improve readability.

summary: Minimal one-line fix guards `args[0]` access with `len(args) > 0`, correctly resolving the IndexError when identify_format is called without positional args. Behavior preserved for all existing cases; standard idiomatic Python.

One-character fix corrects morse_char mapping for '1' from invalid '----' to correct '.----'; char_morse is derived from morse_char via dict comprehension so the reverse mapping updates automatically. Minimal, correct, matches the issue.
Fix correctly converts DataArray to Dataset via to_dataset() before merge, resolving reported AttributeError. Minimal, correct, matches top-level merge() behavior.

issues.description: Docstring for `other` param not updated to mention DataArray support despite type hint change.

summary: Fix add substitutions=False before loop, resolve UnboundLocalError when max_post_process_passes=0. Correct, minimal, matches root cause.

The dedup-by-name-on-first-yield approach stops duplicate reporting but yields the intermediate, pre-substitution hashed_name for adjustable files (exactly the base.css case in the bug report), since every adjustable path is already marked processed during the initial single pass and the multi-pass loop's later, corrected hashed_name is then silently dropped. This produces incorrect '<file> as <hash>' output and would feed subclasses (WhiteNoise, S3 backends) the wrong intermediate file instead of the final one, which is the exact regression the original issue warned about.

issues.description: processed_files accumulates every path (including adjustable ones) during the first single pass, so the second loop's substitution passes never yield for those files again — even when later passes change the final hashed_name. Callers (and post_process consumers/subclasses) get the stale first-pass hash rather than the true final hash stored in hashed_files/the manifest.

Dedup-by-first-occurrence is the wrong invariant for this problem; correctness requires reporting the LAST (final, stabilized) hashed_name per adjustable file, not the first. A dict keyed by name updated each pass and yielded once after the loop settles would give correct behavior; the set-based first-seen approach is a structurally incorrect fix, not merely a style issue.

summary: Minimal one-line fix correctly resolves proxy model's _meta to the concrete model's _meta, matching Django's actual accepted fix for this ticket. Change is narrowly scoped to the exact root cause with no regression risk since concrete_model is a no-op for non-proxy models.

Replaces manual path concatenation with request.get_full_path(force_append_slash=True), which correctly appends the slash before the query string and preserves it. This mirrors how CommonMiddleware handles APPEND_SLASH and fully resolves the reported issue.

Minimal, correct fix replacing the `__file__`-based `python -m django` detection with the documented `__main__.__spec__.parent` check, which also generalizes to any `-m pkg` and avoids `__file__` (unset in some environments). This is the canonical, well-reasoned resolution and is safe to merge.

issues.description: Behavior change: previously only `python -m django` was rebuilt; now any `-m pkg` launch is reconstructed with `-m <parent>`. This is the intended improvement and matches the documented `__spec__` semantics, but slightly broadens reload behavior versus the old narrow check.

Comment added is adequate, but does not explicitly note that `__spec__.parent` is empty (falsy) when launched via a directory/zipfile path, which is why the `and __main__.__spec__.parent` guard matters; a one-line note would aid future readers.

summary: Correct, minimal one-line fix that preserves a caller-supplied empty_label when radio_fields is set, falling back to _('None') only when unset. Resolves the reported issue without regression risk.

issues.description: Uses single quotes (kwargs.get('empty_label'), _('None')) while the surrounding code and Django's Black style use double quotes; Black would reformat to double quotes.

`or` treats an intentionally empty-string empty_label as falsy and replaces it with _('None'); an explicit `'empty_label' in kwargs` check would be stricter, though this edge case is negligible in practice.

summary: Clean, minimal refactor extracting result-serialization into an overridable serialize_result() method; preserves existing behavior exactly and matches the issue's requested design.

issues.description: Docstring updated only in get(); serialize_result() docstring doesn't mention override use-case explicitly, though brief note is adequate.

summary: Correct and general fix: replaces the buggy variable-length tuple return with a proper 2-tuple, using is_dimensionless to map a dimensionless function argument to Dimension(1), resolving the exp() case. Matches sympy conventions; only trivial noise in the diff.

issues.description: Second hunk removes and re-adds the identical get_units_non_prefixed filter line (likely a whitespace-only change) — unrelated noise that should be dropped from the diff.
No inline comment explaining why an all-dimensionless argument set collapses to Dimension(1) while mixed/non-dimensionless args fall through to expr.func over the dimensions.

summary: One-line fix adds response.raise_for_status() before anchor check, causing HTTP error status codes to surface as the actual error instead of a misleading 'Anchor not found' message. Matches the reported expected behavior and reuses the existing exception-handling path in check_uri.

issues.description: This GET request duplicates a prior HEAD/GET status check already performed earlier in check_uri; raise_for_status() here re-validates status on the anchor-fetch response rather than reusing an earlier check, but this is consistent with existing code structure and not a real regression.

summary: Fix correctly avoids axes.set_prop_cycle so CN color references work and the global cycler is no longer mutated, resolving the core issue. However it replaces the cycler-based iteration with a plain iter(colors), silently dropping the documented behavior that a shorter colors list repeats/cycles through the stacked layers.

issues.description: stackplot's colors docstring states the sequence need not match the number of series and will repeat from the beginning. Using iter(colors) instead of itertools.cycle(colors) means once colors is exhausted, next(color_cycle) raises an uncaught StopIteration instead of cycling, breaking documented behavior for any colors list shorter than the number of stacked layers.
next(color_cycle) if color_cycle else ... relies on iterator truthiness pattern; using itertools.cycle would be the more idiomatic and correct fix matching the original cycling semantics.

summary: Fix correctly scopes the post_init signal connection to only occur when width_field or height_field is set, resolving the performance issue without altering behavior when dimension fields are used.

One-line addition of Combinable.MOD to the numeric-type combination registry, mirroring SUB/MUL/DIV so MOD resolves Decimal+Integer to Decimal like other arithmetic operators. Correct, minimal, idiomatic fix that fully addresses the issue.

Refactor of `_check_list_display_item` correctly removes the faulty `hasattr(obj.model, item)` gate so `get_field` is always attempted, matching the issue's correct-behavior table and resolving the false E108 on instance-only descriptor fields (e.g. PositionField). Logic is sound, minimal, and the E108/E109 messages are preserved.

issues.description: The E108 message string is re-wrapped across multiple source lines; harmless and idiomatic, but a trivial readability churn within the diff.

summary: Clean simplification replacing temp .pgpass file + PGPASSFILE with PGPASSWORD env var and subprocess.run, matching the issue request. Correctly resolves the problem with no regression; this mirrors the actual upstream-accepted approach.

issues.description: subprocess.check_call -> subprocess.run drops check=True, so a non-zero psql exit no longer raises CalledProcessError. Acceptable for an interactive dbshell (exit codes are user-driven), but it is a silent behavioral change worth noting.

PGPASSWORD is slightly less secure than a 0600 .pgpass file (env visible via ps to same-user processes on some OSes) and drops the prior UnicodeEncodeError fallback to manual entry. Known, accepted tradeoff; not merge-blocking.

summary: Correct, minimal fix mirroring the real Django resolution for #34768: detects aggregates referencing window-function annotations and routes them through the outer-query/subquery wrapping path, avoiding the Postgres 'aggregate function calls cannot contain window function calls' error. No correctness, regression, or compatibility concerns.

issues.description: The getattr default for contains_over_clause is True (vs False used for the adjacent subquery check). This conservative 'assume window present when attribute missing' default is intentional but non-obvious and would benefit from a brief inline comment.

summary: One-line fix removes erroneous parens from property index entry text in PyMethod.get_index_text, correctly matching PyProperty's index format for property attributes.

One-line fix converts boolean weights to float before computing sum_of_weights, correctly resolving the boolean dot-product bug. Minimal, targeted, and general — addresses root cause for all boolean weight cases, not just the test.

Minimal one-line fix restricts monotonic-check to actually concatenated dims (concat_dims) instead of all dims, correctly resolving issue where identical non-varying coords wrongly required monotonicity.

issues.description: Comment split awkwardly across two lines ('only for dimensions that were combined.' appended after existing comment) - slightly odd phrasing but clear enough.

summary: Clean refactor extracting the non-database-attribute list into a Field.non_db_attrs class attribute and adding 'choices', correctly making AlterField a noop on SQLite when only choices change. Matches established Django design and resolves the issue generally, not just for the test case.

issues.description: New public-ish Field.non_db_attrs attribute is an extension point (subclasses/3rd-party fields can override) but gets only an inline comment; a brief note in docs would help, though not merge-blocking.

summary: Removes the hard-coded dashoffset=0 override so patches honor the dash tuple offset, matching Line2D behavior and correctly fixing the reported bug. Functionally correct; only cosmetic leftovers remain.

issues.description: The `cbook._setattr_cm(self, _dash_pattern=self._dash_pattern)` now sets the attribute to its own current value, making the context manager a no-op wrapper. Cleaner to drop the _dash_pattern override entirely and keep only `_bind_draw_path_function`. Harmless but dead structure.
Redundant parentheses in `(self._dash_pattern)` — should be plain `self._dash_pattern`. Pure style nit.

Old explanatory comment removed with no replacement noting the intentional behavior change; a brief note (or changelog/whatsnew entry) would help future maintainers understand the now-respected offset.

summary: Fix replaces unescape+length-math with a char-by-char strip loop that never strips ';', which does resolve the entity-splitting bug but as a side effect disables trimming of literal (non-entity) trailing semicolons that TRAILING_PUNCTUATION_CHARS was also meant to catch, e.g. 'example.com;' no longer trims the semicolon into trail.

issues.description: TRAILING_PUNCTUATION_CHARS includes ';' for legitimate cases like a URL followed by a real semicolon in prose. The new loop's blanket guard 'middle[-1] != ";"' skips stripping any time the last char is ';', even when it is not part of an HTML entity, so a real trailing semicolon (e.g. 'example.com;') stays attached to the URL/link text instead of being moved to trail as before.

Approach special-cases ';' globally rather than distinguishing 'part of an unescaped entity' from 'standalone punctuation character', so it trades one correctness bug for another instead of a fully general fix.

summary: Patch passes already-computed self.prog_name to CommandParser, correctly fixing usage/error output to honor the argv passed to ManagementUtility rather than sys.argv[0]. Minimal, targeted, matches the issue's recommended fix.

Adds a clean get_inlines() hook that get_inline_instances() now calls, exactly matching the issue request and Django's established get_*() override pattern. Backward compatible since default returns self.inlines, preserving existing behavior.

issues.description: No docstring on get_inlines() and admin docs/release notes not shown in diff; maintainers typically pair such hooks with docs, but this is non-blocking for the source change.

summary: One-line change swaps `_default_manager` for `_base_manager` in ForeignKey.validate(), which is exactly the fix the issue requests and matches Django's accepted resolution. Minimal, correct, and uses the right abstraction; no merge-blocking problems.

issues.description: Subtle behavior change: validation no longer applies the default manager's filters, so projects that relied on default-manager scoping during FK validation see different results. This is the intended fix and well-documented in the issue, but warrants a release note mention.
No accompanying docs/release-note update in the diff to flag the validation-manager change for users; maintainers typically add a short note, though not merge-blocking.

summary: The patch wires up the previously-ignored tzinfo, but resolves the zone name via self.tzinfo.tzname(None), which is a fragile approach that diverges from the project's existing get_tzname() helper. For common tzinfo types this yields an abbreviation/LMT/None rather than the IANA zone name, producing wrong or no-op results outside the narrow case exercised by the test.

issues.description: self.tzinfo.tzname(None) is the wrong abstraction for deriving a DB timezone name. tzname() is DST/datetime-dependent: for a pytz zone the un-localized instance returns a stale abbreviation/LMT, for zoneinfo.ZoneInfo it returns None (so the conversion is silently skipped and the bug is NOT fixed), and for a fixed-offset datetime.timezone it returns 'UTC-05:00'-style strings that are not valid DB timezone identifiers. Passing an abbreviation like 'EST' to AT TIME ZONE drops DST handling and gives incorrect dates for half the year. Django already has the TimeZone mixin's get_tzname()/timezone._g

Incomplete: the inline branch does not handle a tzinfo passed as a string and does not work for zoneinfo-based timezones (tzname(None) -> None), so the stated goal ('pass in any tzinfo / America_New_York while app is UTC') is only met for the specific timezone object type used by the repro test.

Logic is duplicated inline in two as_sql() methods as a dense nested ternary rather than reusing the existing get_tzname() helper, hurting readability and risking divergence between TruncDate/TruncTime and the rest of the TimeZone mixin.

summary: Patch resolves the reported TypeError by stripping non-numeric (dev/rc) suffixes from the requested `version` before LooseVersion comparison, which fixes the issue as filed. It only sanitizes the `version` argument, not the installed `have_version`, so a symmetric failure can still occur when the installed module is itself a dev build positionally conflicting with a numeric required version.

issues.description: Only `version` is sanitized; `have_version` is left untouched. LooseVersion's TypeError is symmetric, so e.g. minversion('numpy','1.14.3') with an installed dev build like '1.14.dev1' still raises TypeError. Since minversion's core job is comparing the installed version, the fix is incomplete for dev-install environments (common in astropy's own CI/dev usage).

Stripping '1.14dev' to '1.14' silently loses prerelease ordering (a 1.14dev requirement becomes stricter, equal to 1.14). Acceptable approximation but changes semantics for prerelease-vs-prerelease comparisons.

Regex literal is uncommented as to why epoch is included but local/post segments are dropped; relies on re.match prefix semantics implicitly. Readable enough given the cited PEP440 reference, but the partial-match intent could be clearer.

summary: Change guards the widget-defaulting block with `if 'widget' not in kwargs`, mirroring the existing pattern in formfield_for_foreignkey() and correctly letting callers override the widget. Minimal, correct, and idiomatic for the repo.

Correctly removes unnecessary np.abs from window normalization, matching scipy's implementation and fixing wrong scaling for windows with negative values (e.g. flattop). Minimal, targeted, and correct.

Adds an n_SV==0 guard that avoids the division-by-zero when building dual_coef_indptr, setting dual_coef_ to an empty sparse matrix exactly as the issue expects. Correct, minimal, matches the documented expected result.

issues.description: dual_coef_indices = np.tile(np.arange(n_SV), n_class) is still computed before the guard but is unused in the empty branch; could move it into the else for cleanliness. Negligible (empty array), not blocking.
No inline comment explaining why the empty-support-vector case needs special handling; a one-line note would aid future maintainers. Nit only.

summary: The patch correctly generalizes the valid-element count to multiple dims (np.take(mask.shape, axis).prod()), but it folds the array-masking branch under `if hasattr(axis, "__len__")`, so single-dimension reductions (integer axis) no longer hit it and fall through to the scalar `elif` branch — silently breaking per-element min_count masking for the common single-dim case. The correct fix keeps the `if axis is not None and getattr(result, "ndim", False)` gate and only swaps `mask.shape[axis]` for `np.take(mask.shape, axis).prod()`.

issues.description: Regression for single-dim min_count. For an integer axis (e.g. da.sum("dim_0", min_count=2)), `hasattr(axis, "__len__")` is False, so execution skips the array-masking branch and hits `elif`, which only compares the TOTAL valid count (mask.size - mask.sum()) against min_count. Per-column masking is lost: input [[1,nan,3],[nan,nan,6]].sum("dim_0", min_count=2) returns [1,0,9] instead of the correct [nan,nan,9]. Previously this worked via the now-deleted `if axis is not None and getattr(result, "ndim", False)` branch.

Wrong integration of the right idea. np.take(mask.shape, axis).prod() is correct and works for both int and tuple axis, but it was placed under the `hasattr(axis, "__len__")` (tuple/list only) condition. It should replace `mask.shape[axis]` while keeping the original `if axis is not None and getattr(result, "ndim", False)` gate, which covers both single- and multi-dim array results.

Fix is incomplete/asymmetric: it only repairs the multi-dim-to-scalar path shown in the issue while regressing the single-dim-to-array path. The reproduction example da.sum(["dim_0","dim_1"], min_count=1) passes, but the broader min_count contract is no longer honored.

summary: Cast to int64 fixes the int32 overflow at the root, and rewriting `tk/sqrt(pk*qk)` as `sqrt(tk/pk)*sqrt(tk/qk)` avoids the large intermediate product while being mathematically equivalent for non-negative tk/pk/qk. Minimal, correct, targeted fix.

issues.description: No inline comment explaining why the formula was rewritten (overflow avoidance); future readers may 'simplify' it back to tk/sqrt(pk*qk) and reintroduce the bug.
Reordered formula introduces a second sqrt + float roundoff path; negligible numerically and the int64 cast already prevents overflow, so the dual-sqrt form is slightly redundant but harmless.

summary: Fix correctly wraps fcntl.flock calls in try/except OSError, matching Python's documented flock semantics (None on success, OSError on failure) and resolving the reported always-False bug.

Patch fixes the migrate symptom by flushing after every OutputWrapper.write(), but takes the wrong approach: the actual bug is that OutputWrapper.flush() is a TextIOBase no-op (never delegates to self._out), and forcing a flush on every write introduces a real performance regression for high-volume commands. Django's accepted fix overrides flush() instead.

issues.description: Wrong abstraction. Root cause is OutputWrapper inheriting TextIOBase.flush() (a no-op) which shadows delegation to self._out, so explicit self.stdout.flush() calls do nothing. Correct fix overrides flush() to call self._out.flush(); flushing inside write() instead is heavy-handed and side-steps the actual defect.

Reported issue title is 'flush() ... doesn't work'. This patch never makes the flush() method itself work — explicit self.stdout.flush()/self.stderr.flush() calls remain TextIOBase no-ops. Only the migrate progressive-output symptom is patched, not the named API.

Unconditional self._out.flush() on every write penalizes high-throughput commands (e.g. dumpdata writing many records to a redirected file/pipe), turning block-buffered output into per-write flushes. Avoidable inefficiency that the flush()-override approach does not incur.
No guard for streams lacking flush(); a custom self._out without a working flush could raise, where the safer fix uses hasattr(self._out, 'flush').

summary: Fix correctly guards zero-support-vector case in sparse SVM fit, matching dense-path behavior; minimal and correct.

One-line fix wraps `variable_attrs[0]` in `dict()` so combine_attrs='override' returns a copy instead of a reference, exactly matching the issue's root cause and consistent with the no_conflicts/other branches. Minimal, correct, mergeable.

issues.description: dict() is a shallow copy, so nested/mutable attr values remain shared between source and merged product. Matches behavior of the sibling combine_attrs branches, so consistent and not a regression — minor caveat only.

summary: Adds a minimal, correctly-placed empty-name guard for Blueprint that raises ValueError before the dot check, fully resolving the reported issue. Approach matches the adjacent existing validation idiom; no correctness or compatibility concerns.

issues.description: Second hunk re-touches `return f` (trailing whitespace/newline normalization) unrelated to the fix — trivial scope noise, not blocking.

summary: The unsigned→signed data conversion for `_Unsigned=False` is correct and the values now decode properly, but the `warnings.warn` call ends up inside the new `elif` branch (16-space indent, no `else`), so it fires the misleading 'not of integer type, ignoring attribute' warning right after a successful conversion and is no longer emitted for genuinely non-integer `_Unsigned` variables.

issues.description: The unchanged `warnings.warn(...)` context line sits at the same indent as the new `signed_dtype` body, so it is now part of the `elif data.dtype.kind == 'u' and unsigned == 'false':` block. After correctly converting u→i it STILL emits 'variable %r has _Unsigned attribute but is not of integer type. Ignoring attribute.' — directly contradicting the action taken. Since the warning was the exact symptom reported in the issue, the user's pydap case keeps seeing the SerializationWarning even though values are now right. The warning should live in a separate `else:` branch (i.e. `if kind=='i': ...

By absorbing the former `else: warn` into the `elif`, the original warning for legitimately unsupported `_Unsigned` cases (e.g. float dtype carrying an `_Unsigned` attribute, the case shown in the issue's `engine='pydap'` float32 example) is dropped — those now decode silently with no diagnostic, a behavioral regression versus the prior code.
No inline comment documents the `_Unsigned=False` OPeNDAP/netCDF-c 'hack' being handled here; a one-line comment referencing the convention would aid future maintainers.

summary: Minimal one-line fix guards imaginary-coordinate validation behind the `evaluate` flag, consistent with how evaluate=False defers other checks/simplifications elsewhere in sympy, and directly resolves the reported crash.

issues.description: With evaluate=False, a Point can now be constructed with genuinely imaginary coordinates without raising; acceptable since evaluate=False intentionally defers validation/evaluation, but worth noting as a behavior change from strict pre-patch validation.

summary: Adds AddIndex.reduce to cancel a matching AddIndex/RemoveIndex pair during migration optimization, matching Django's established reduce() pattern. Correct, minimal fix; index names are globally unique so omitting a model_name check is safe.

issues.description: Only handles AddIndex+RemoveIndex cancellation. Other reducible pairs (e.g. RemoveIndex+AddIndex, RenameIndex interactions) not covered, but those are out of scope for the stated issue and can land separately.

summary: Reordering the zero-check after the Boolean/Number-specific branches correctly makes Float.__eq__ short-circuit to False for Boolean comparisons before the truthy/falsy shortcut can fire, fixing the S(0.0)==S.false inconsistency without altering behavior for Number, NumberSymbol, or other object comparisons.

issues.description: No comment explaining why the zero-check must come after the Boolean/Number branches; a future editor could reorder it back and reintroduce the bug.

summary: Correct, minimal fix: swaps only `top`/`bottom` grouping in the shared `_get_aligned_offsets` helper, resolving the reversed HPacker alignment while leaving `left`/`right` (used by VPacker), `center`, and `baseline` untouched. Matches the actual upstream resolution.

issues.description: Helper still lacks a brief comment explaining why `left`+`bottom` and `right`+`top` are grouped together (the dual VPacker/HPacker coordinate mapping that caused the original mistake), which would guard against a future re-reversal. Non-blocking nit.

summary: Fix makes the n_jobs==1 path derive a per-run seed via random_state.randint and a fresh check_random_state, mirroring the parallel path so sequential and parallel runs consume randomness identically and yield the same inertia. Correct, minimal, and resolves the reported discrepancy.

issues.description: `zip(range(n_init), seeds)` is redundant; `enumerate(seeds)` is cleaner. Also the loop variable `it` is unused in the body, same as before the change.

summary: Fix correctly resolves the reported crash by special-casing OrderBy instances in Meta.ordering, but it's narrower than needed: any other resolve_expression-bearing item (e.g. bare F() or Func()) in Meta.ordering will still hit the string-oriented recursive path and crash the same way.

issues.description: Only isinstance(item, OrderBy) is special-cased; other expression types with resolve_expression (F(), Func(), Case(), etc.) placed in Meta.ordering still fall through to find_ordering_name's string-splitting logic and will raise the same class of error, so the general expression-ordering case isn't fully fixed.

Hard-coding is_ref=False for every OrderBy item is a simplification; if such an item ever legitimately referenced an annotated alias, downstream logic that branches on is_ref would silently treat it as non-referential.

summary: The middle hunk correctly fixes the issue by adding Combinable.MOD to the different-type numeric operand block, which is the actual fix needed. However, the first and third hunks each add a duplicate Combinable.MOD to tuples that already contain it — functionally harmless (dict-comprehension keys dedupe) but clearly erroneous and would not be merged as-is.

issues.description: Two of the three added lines are redundant duplicates: Combinable.MOD is appended to connector tuples in the same-type block and the field_type-comprehension block where MOD is ALREADY present. Only the middle insertion (different-type operands) is the real fix. The duplicates pollute the diff and signal a misunderstanding; a maintainer would require their removal before merge.
Duplicate enum entries in a tuple iterated by a dict comprehension are confusing to future readers even though they have no runtime effect (key overwritten with identical value).

summary: One-line fix correctly propagates `cls` into the recursive call so nested iterables of name-strings build the requested class (e.g. Function) instead of defaulting to Symbol. Minimal, correct, and resolves the reported issue without regression risk.

Fix removes incorrect np.abs() calls in window normalization, aligning with scipy's reference implementation; correctly resolves the flattop-window bug without altering behavior for non-negative windows.

The patch fixes the reported symmetric sum-of-even-powers case, but instead of forwarding `permute` to the recursive `diophantine(eq, param)` call it reimplements permutation handling by blindly applying `signed_permutations` to every solution. That diverges from diophantine's type-specific permute logic and will yield incorrect/spurious solutions for non-symmetric equation types (e.g. binary_quadratic) when syms order differs.

issues.description: `signed_permutations` (all orderings + all sign flips) is applied unconditionally regardless of equation type. diophantine's normal permute path is type-dependent: some types only permute signs, some only under validity checks (e.g. permute_signs_check for binary_quadratic). For asymmetric equations like x**2 + 2*y**2 = c, blindly permuting order/signs produces invalid (non-solution) tuples. The recursive call still drops `permute`; the correct minimal fix is to forward it: `diophantine(eq, param, permute=permute)`.

Regression risk: for any equation type other than the symmetric general_sum_of_squares/general_sum_of_even_powers, the syms-reorder + permute=True branch now returns a different (over-generated, partly invalid) result set than the canonical permute path would, because the per-type permutation rules are bypassed.
Fix is overfit to the reported n**4+m**4 case (where signed_permutations happens to equal the correct type-specific permutation) rather than reusing the existing general permute machinery.
Non-minimal: replaces a concise comprehension with an explicit loop and reimplemented permutation logic where a one-token `permute=permute` argument on the recursion suffices.

summary: One-line guard `step is not None` correctly stops `has_fit_parameter(None, ...)` from triggering the `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'fit'` when a dropped estimator is combined with sample_weight. Minimal, correct, root-cause fix matching repo idiom; None estimators are already filtered downstream in actual fitting.

One-line change computes the square-free norm on the original polynomial F instead of the square-free part f, which correctly recovers the factor that was being dropped over algebraic extensions; this matches the real upstream fix and resolves the reported issue. Mergeable as a minimal, targeted correctness fix.

issues.description: dmp_sqf_norm now receives F (the original, possibly non-square-free) rather than the square-free part f. Its shift loop searches for a square-free norm; a non-square-free input could change termination/iteration behavior or cost. The reported case z=(x-1)*(y-1) is already square-free so it is unaffected, but inputs with repeated factors over an extension (e.g. (x-1)**2*(y-1)) should be confirmed not to regress. Tests pass, so not blocking, but worth a covering test.

The fix likely works around incorrect behavior of multivariate dmp_sqf_part (which appears to drop the y-1 factor) rather than addressing that root cause directly. Computing the norm on F is itself legitimate (multiplicities are recovered later via dmp_trial_division), but the underlying sqf_part discrepancy may still surface in other code paths.

No comment explains why the norm is intentionally computed on F while f (the square-free part) is still kept for the len(factors)==1 branch. The f-vs-F distinction is subtle and a short comment would prevent a future maintainer from 'simplifying' it back to f.

summary: The fix correctly replaces `max(powers.values())` (largest single-variable exponent) with `sum(powers.values())` (true total degree), matching the documented `min_degree <= total_degree(monom) <= max_degree` contract. Minimal, correct, symmetric across the commutative and non-commutative branches.

issues.description: No inline comment added explaining that total degree = sum of exponents; a one-line note would aid future readers, but not merge-blocking.

summary: Correct, minimal one-line fix that resolves the broken PasswordResetForm link by building the relative URL from the actual pk (`../../{pk}/password/`) instead of assuming the URL segment is the pk. Preserves behavior in the normal pk-based case and fixes the to_field (e.g. uuid) 404 case.
Correct, minimal fix — replaces manual __name__/__doc__ copying with functools.wraps, resolving inspect.signature() returning wrong signature on manager methods.

Fix correctly resolves the issue: constructor now allows non-disjoint cycles (across-cycle duplicates) while still rejecting duplicates in non-cycle array-form input, matching the requested behavior of identity permutation from [[0,1],[0,1]].

issues.description: Duplicate-check is now entirely skipped for is_cycle=True, since it operates on the flattened list of all cycle args; this also silently permits a malformed duplicate within a single cycle (e.g. Permutation([[0,1,0]])) rather than only permitting duplicates across separate cycles. Edge case, not the scenario in the bug report.

summary: Minimal, correct fix adding AlterField-on-AlterField reduction to AlterField.reduce, matching the issue's suggested approach and Django's reduce-pattern conventions. Returns the later operation when the field operation targets the same model/field, which correctly collapses chained AlterFields.

issues.description: The new `elif` line exceeds Django's typical formatting; black would wrap the `isinstance(...) and self.is_same_field_operation(operation)` condition across lines as the surrounding code does. Cosmetic only, not merge-blocking.

summary: One-line fix changes `return variable_attrs[0]` to `return dict(variable_attrs[0])`, making `combine_attrs='override'` return a copy instead of a reference, exactly matching the pattern already used by the other combine_attrs branches. Correctly and minimally resolves the reported aliasing bug.

issues.description: dict() is a shallow copy, so nested mutable attr values remain shared between source and merged product. This matches the behavior of the other combine_attrs branches (e.g. no_conflicts also uses dict()), so it is consistent and not a regression, but deep mutation of nested attrs would still alias.

summary: Correct, minimal fix: AlterField.reduce now collapses a subsequent same-field AlterField by returning the later operation, matching the issue's proposal and standard reduce semantics where a later AlterField fully replaces the field definition. Matches Django's actual merged fix for this ticket.

Minimal, correct change adding params={'value': value} to the ModelChoiceField invalid_choice ValidationError, matching how ChoiceField and ModelMultipleChoiceField already supply the value. Mirrors the approach Django actually merged for this ticket.

issues.description: The default 'invalid_choice' message for ModelChoiceField still reads 'That choice is not one of the available choices.' and contains no %(value)s placeholder, so out of the box the value is not displayed; the params only take effect for custom/overridden messages. This is an intentional backward-compatible tradeoff (matches Django's merged fix) but means the literal issue request to 'modify the default error message' is not fully satisfied.

summary: Adds `_print_Indexed` to PythonCodePrinter, exactly resolving the issue. Correct, minimal, idiomatic; matches printer method conventions.

issues.description: Uses str(base) instead of self._print(base) for the base; fine for IndexedBase but slightly less general than dispatching the base through the printer. Not a merge blocker.

summary: Minimal fix mirrors common sympy idiom (Matrix, Add, etc.) of treating literal 0 as additive identity before invoking the vector-specific type check, resolving the reported sum() TypeError.

issues.description: other == 0 relies on Vector.__eq__ tolerating comparison with a non-Vector int without raising; correct here since sympy operations are designed for this, but slightly implicit.

summary: Correctly broadens the InheritDocstrings type check from `inspect.isfunction` to also include `inspect.isdatadescriptor`, which matches property objects and resolves the reported issue with a minimal, general fix. The only extra change is harmless removal of stray blank lines.

issues.description: Removal of blank lines after the module docstring and before `__all__` is unrelated whitespace cleanup, slightly outside the scope of the property fix, but cosmetically harmless.

`inspect.isdatadescriptor` matches all data descriptors (property + objects with __get__/__set__), not only properties; this is the intended generalization and the public-member + `__doc__ is None` filters keep it safe, but it is slightly broader than the literal issue.

summary: Fix correctly extends call_command's required-argument passthrough to also cover options belonging to a required mutually exclusive group, matching the root cause in the issue. Approach mirrors existing style in the same function (walking parser._actions/private argparse internals), is minimal, and doesn't alter behavior for non-group required arguments.

issues.description: Relies on argparse private attribute parser._mutually_exclusive_groups/_group_actions, but this is consistent with the surrounding code's existing use of opt._long_opts-style private argparse internals in the same function.

summary: The one-character sign fix to m12 (2*s*(q.c*q.d - q.b*q.a)) corrects the quaternion-to-rotation-matrix derivation to match the standard formula, producing a proper rotation about the x-axis for the reported example. Change is minimal and correct.

issues.description: Second diff hunk re-touches the final return/EOF line with no semantic change (whitespace/newline only); cosmetic noise, not a real problem.

summary: Fix correctly replaces raw str() interpolation with self._print() in _print_Limit and _print_Rel so nested printer settings (e.g. sympy_integers) propagate, matching the issue's root cause. Minimal, targeted, consistent with existing StrPrinter idioms.

Fix correctly special-cases empty input before the numlike-check/deprecation-warning path, avoiding both the spurious warning and the downstream ConversionError while leaving non-empty behavior unchanged.

issues.description: Wrapping the whole original body in an else block adds a level of indentation instead of using an early return, slightly increasing nesting without functional cost.

summary: Correctly fixes the bug: any non-ASCII string now always goes through NFKD normalization and combining-char stripping, so already-NFKD inputs like 'n'+COMBINING TILDE are now stripped. The ASCII fast-path is a clean equivalent of the old early-return and also avoids the list comprehension, with no regression.

One-line fix adds deepcopy of error_messages dict in Field.__deepcopy__, correctly resolving shared-dict bug between copied fields. Minimal, idiomatic, matches existing pattern (widget deepcopy, validators slice copy).
Small targeted fix computes correct display address for the '0' shorthand case, matching documented behavior without altering underlying bind logic.

issues.description: Mixes f-string formatting for the new addr variable with the surrounding code's older %-style formatting elsewhere, a minor style inconsistency.

summary: Correctly moves use_required_attribute logic to FileInput so required is suppressed when initial data exists, matching the issue request. Adding an identical override to ClearableFileInput is redundant since it now inherits the same method from FileInput, but this is a trivial nit and does not block merge.

issues.description: ClearableFileInput.use_required_attribute is now an exact duplicate of the inherited FileInput.use_required_attribute and can be removed; the issue only asked to move it to the FileInput base class.

summary: Adds a guard returning self when the right-hand operand equals zero, correctly fixing sum()/0+Vector addition; matches a previously commented-out fix in the same file and is minimal and safe.

issues.description: Using `other == 0` before type-checking could raise/behave oddly for exotic right-hand operands whose __eq__ doesn't tolerate comparison to int 0, though this is consistent with existing sympy idioms.

summary: The patch correctly adds self.save_m2m() to persist ManyToMany data, but does so in a second redundant `if commit:` block that calls user.save() a second time, so the user is saved twice. The fix should have added save_m2m() to the existing if-block instead.

issues.description: Wrong implementation: a duplicate `if commit:` block was appended instead of editing the existing one. Result is two consecutive `user.save()` calls, saving the user twice on every commit. Correct fix adds only `self.save_m2m()` to the existing block.

Behavioral regression: redundant second user.save() triggers extra signals (pre_save/post_save) and a second DB write/UPDATE on every UserCreationForm.save(commit=True), changing observable side-effect behavior.
Performance: avoidable duplicate database write per save() call.
Two identical adjacent `if commit:` blocks is unclear and clearly unintended structure.

summary: One-line change setting the default FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS to 0o644 correctly resolves the inconsistent-permissions issue between MemoryUploadedFile and TemporaryUploadedFile paths; this is the minimal, correct fix. The only caveat is that it's a backward-incompatible default change that should be accompanied by release notes (in files not shown in this source-only diff).

issues.description: Changing the default from None to 0o644 alters file permissions for projects that did not set FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS explicitly and relied on the previous (size-dependent) behavior. This is an intentional, correct fix but is a backward-incompatible behavior change.

A default-settings change of this kind normally warrants a release-note / docs entry flagging the backward-incompatibility. Not visible in the source-only diff, so may already be handled, but worth confirming before merge.

summary: Fix correctly passes bin_range into hist_kwargs so density renormalization respects range param instead of dropping it, matching root cause identified in bisect to #8638.

issues.description: Only covers density-and-not-stacked branch; stacked+density path not touched by this diff, though issue report doesn't demonstrate that case is broken.

summary: Correct, minimal fix: leaf nodes carry feature index TREE_UNDEFINED (-2), and feature_names[-2] raised IndexError only when fewer than 2 feature names existed; guarding with TREE_UNDEFINED resolves the crash generally since feature_names_ entries for leaves are never actually used in rendering. The second hunk is a no-op trailing-newline change.

issues.description: Inconsistency: with feature_names provided, leaf entries become 'undefined', but the else branch still yields 'feature_-2' for leaves. Harmless since leaf entries are never rendered, but the two paths now differ.
Second hunk only changes the final line's trailing newline with no functional effect; trivial noise in the diff.

summary: Adds symmetric handling for the netCDF-c/thredds '_Unsigned=False' hack on already-unsigned data, mirroring the existing signed->unsigned branch. Change is minimal, consistent with the surrounding code's structure and conventions, and does not alter unrelated behavior.

issues.description: Duplicates the fill-value/transform logic pattern from the sibling branch instead of factoring a shared helper; acceptable given the existing code already has this shape.

summary: Minimal, correct fix that guards MaxLengthValidator creation on a non-null max_length, matching the existing BinaryField.__init__ precedent and removing the broken validator on bare CharField() output fields. No correctness, regression, or compatibility concerns.

issues.description: Concrete CharField model definitions without max_length now silently skip the MaxLengthValidator, but they are already rejected at system-check time (fields.E120), so user-facing behavior is unchanged; worth a mental note but not a regression.

summary: Adds a minimal, correctly-placed guard raising ValueError on empty Blueprint name, directly resolving the reported issue without side effects. Consistent with the adjacent dot-character validation in style and message format.

Patch resolves the boolean-X TypeError by casting X to float, but places the cast inside `_huber_loss_and_gradient`, which the L-BFGS optimizer calls repeatedly, so X is re-copied to float64 on every iteration. Correct fix belongs in `fit` via `check_X_y(..., dtype=[np.float64, np.float32])`, matching `LinearRegression`.

issues.description: `X = X.astype(float)` runs inside the loss/gradient function called once per optimizer iteration, allocating a fresh float64 copy of X each call. Avoidable repeated allocation; should cast once in `fit`.

Wrong location for the fix. sklearn idiom is to validate/coerce dtype in `fit` via `check_X_y`/`check_array`; coercing deep inside the numeric kernel is fragile and inconsistent with other estimators.
`astype(float)` forces float64, silently upcasting a float32 X (extra memory, lost dtype intent) rather than preserving supported float dtypes as check_X_y dtype list would.
Trailing whitespace on the blank comment line and inline coercion deviate from repo style/validation conventions.

summary: Patch moves the check_changes early-exit before migration writing, so makemigrations --check now exits without writing files, matching migrate --check and optimizemigration --check. Correct, minimal fix that resolves the issue cleanly.

Adds a clean, minimal get_inlines() hook and routes get_inline_instances() through it, correctly resolving the issue without behavioral change to default usage. Mergeable; only minor convention nit on the signature default.

issues.description: get_inlines(self, request, obj) lacks the obj=None default used by sibling hooks (get_fieldsets, get_fields, get_ordering). Internally always called with obj so works, but inconsistent for subclasses calling it directly.
No docs update (ref/contrib/admin) for the new public hook; docstring is present but a maintainer would typically add release notes/docs.

summary: One-line fix correctly passes engine's autoescape setting to the Context constructor in render_to_string, matching Django's existing autoescape handling elsewhere.

Adds update_wrapper(bound_method, method) so the partial passed to decorators carries __name__/__module__/__dict__, directly fixing the reported AttributeError. This is the minimal, correct fix and matches the canonical upstream resolution.

issues.description: No inline comment explains why update_wrapper is needed on the partial (to restore __name__ etc. that decorators like @wraps expect); a one-line comment would aid future readers, but surrounding context already discusses the partial so this is optional.

summary: Minimal, correct fix that catches ValueError (from max() on an empty sequence when items() is empty) alongside the existing TypeError, matching the issue's suggested solution. Resolves the reported crash without affecting other behavior.

Correctly resolves the data-loss bug for non-numeric (CharField) primary keys by also treating an empty-string FK attname as 'not yet set' so the saved related object's pk is copied. Targeted and functionally correct; only minor idiom/readability nits.

issues.description: Hardcodes `== ""` instead of the project-idiomatic `getattr(self, field.attname) in field.empty_values`, which would generalize to all empty sentinels and read as more deliberate. Functionally equivalent for FK attnames (integer 0 is unaffected since `0 == ""` is False), so not blocking, but a maintainer would likely prefer the empty_values form.
Calls `getattr(self, field.attname)` twice in the same condition; could bind to a local (e.g. walrus) for clarity and to avoid the redundant lookup. Trivial.

summary: Correct, minimal fix: replaces the too-narrow `isinstance(attr, Expression)` check with the duck-typed `hasattr(attr, 'resolve_expression')`, which is Django's idiomatic marker for expression-like objects and properly handles plain F() (F subclasses Combinable, not Expression). Also drops the now-unused Expression import. No regression, no blocking issues.

issues.description: Duck-typing on `resolve_expression` is theoretically broader than the old isinstance check (any object exposing that attribute is now treated as an expression), but this is the established ORM convention and the new set is a strict superset of the old Expression instances, so no realistic regression. Could narrow to `isinstance(attr, (Expression, F))` if stricter typing preferred, but duck-typing matches the rest of the codebase.

summary: The one-line change from `>` to `>=` fixes the reported mincnt inconsistency for mincnt>=1, but because `mincnt` still defaults to 0 when unspecified, the comparison `len(acc) >= 0` is now always true, so `reduce_C_function` gets invoked on genuinely empty bins instead of being skipped. This crashes for common reduce functions like `np.min`/`np.max` (ValueError on empty array) and produces spurious RuntimeWarnings even for the default `np.mean`, whereas previously empty bins were guaranteed to bypass the reduction entirely.

issues.description: Previously the `>` comparison with default mincnt=0 guaranteed `reduce_C_function` was never called on an empty accumulator (`len(acc) > 0` required at least one point). Switching to `>=` removes that guarantee for the default/unspecified-mincnt case: `len(acc) >= 0` is always true, so empty hex bins are now passed to `reduce_C_function`. For reduce functions that don't tolerate empty input (e.g. `np.max`, `np.min`), this raises a ValueError on any hexbin call with a sparse/non-uniform data distribution and no explicit `mincnt` — a very common usage pattern. Even with the default `np.mean`, it

The fix addresses the mincnt>=1 symmetry with the C-is-None path but does not add a guard (e.g. `len(acc) > 0 and len(acc) >= mincnt`) to preserve the pre-existing invariant that empty bins are excluded before reduction, leaving the empty-bin edge case unresolved.

summary: Fix directly resolves the issue: adds is_path_or_empty validator so empty input on the 'new root path' prompt is accepted, letting the existing sys.exit(1) check fire instead of looping on a validation error. Minimal, targeted change with no regression risk to other prompts.

Wraps the widget-assignment block in formfield_for_manytomany() with `if 'widget' not in kwargs:`, correctly mirroring the existing formfield_for_foreignkey() pattern so a caller-supplied widget is respected. Fix is correct, minimal, and idiomatic; safe to merge.

issues.description: Reflowing the three widget constructors onto multiple lines is incidental formatting unrelated to the fix, but it's cosmetic and consistent with Django style, so non-blocking.

summary: Fix correctly special-cases bytes payload to bypass form-encoding, resolving issue without touching existing str/dict/file-like paths.

issues.description: Only checks isinstance(data, bytes); other binary-like buffer types (bytearray, memoryview) still fall into _encode_params and may break, though not part of reported bug.

summary: One-line fix correctly routes unique-field ADD COLUMN through table-remake path, matching SQLite's inability to ALTER TABLE ADD a UNIQUE column; minimal and targeted at the root cause rather than the specific model in the report.
Fix swaps is_path validator for allow_empty so blank input passes validation, then exits with status 0 instead of 1 for the intentional user-initiated exit. Minimal, targeted, matches issue.

issues.description: Exit code semantics change (1->0) not documented in changelog/comment, though correct since this is a normal exit path not an error.

summary: Patch correctly fixes DateFormat.Y() to zero-pad years below 1000 by formatting with '%04d', matching the documented four-digit behavior. Minimal, targeted change with updated docstring; matches the repo's existing '%02d' idiom used in y(). One subtle return-type change (int → str) is consistent with all other DateFormat methods, which return strings.

issues.description: Return type changes from int to str. This is the correct/intended behavior (all other format specifiers return strings and format() joins them), and the previous int return was the bug, so any code relying on the int was already broken. Non-blocking.

summary: Correct, minimal fix matching the real upstream resolution for #33856: broadening the FK attname check from `is None` to `in field.empty_values` so a non-numeric (CharField) PK assigned empty then saved gets copied onto the parent. No regression for numeric PKs since `0`/`False` are not in `empty_values`.

issues.description: Inline comment still says 'Use pk from related object if it has been saved after an assignment' — fine, but could note the empty-string/empty-value case now covered. Non-blocking nit.

summary: Change replaces incorrect `False` results with `None` when complex-vs-imaginary status is undecided, correctly aligning with is_zero's contract of never returning a wrong answer. Fix is minimal, targeted, and matches the issue's root cause.

issues.description: Added trailing `return None` is redundant since Python already returns None implicitly at end of function; harmless but could be omitted.

summary: Correctly replaces buggy string comparison with semantic version comparison via packaging.version.parse, properly resolving the reported version-ordering bug (0.10 > 0.6). Fix is minimal and behaviorally correct; only a minor style nit on import placement.

issues.description: Import `from packaging.version import parse as parse_version` placed inside the function (within the loop body) rather than at module top, against PEP8/repo convention. Import caching makes the perf cost negligible, but it should be hoisted to module level for readability.

parse_version on a malformed/non-PEP440 version string can raise InvalidVersion, a slightly different failure mode than the old string compare. 'unknown version' is short-circuited so the common case is safe; real extension versions are virtually always PEP440-compliant, so regression risk is low.

summary: One-line fix converts a DataArray `other` into a Dataset via `to_dataset()` before merging, directly resolving the reported AttributeError and mirroring how the top-level `xr.merge()` already handles this case.

issues.description: An unnamed DataArray passed to `ds.merge(da)` will raise a ValueError from `to_dataset()` requiring a name, but this matches the existing behavior of `xr.merge()` for the same input, so it's not a new edge case introduced by this change.

summary: The patch correctly handles the 1-element tuple special case by emitting a trailing comma while preserving empty and multi-element tuple behavior. Clean, minimal, idiomatic change with no correctness or regression concerns.

Adding `__reversed__` returning `reversed(self.dict)` correctly makes OrderedSet reversible; dict preserves insertion order and is reversible in Python 3.8+, matching the existing `__iter__` pattern. Clean, minimal, idiomatic fix that fully resolves the issue.

Minimal, correct fix that normalizes FIXTURE_DIRS entries to strings before the duplicate check, so Path instances (and mixed Path/str pointing to the same dir) are now detected as duplicates. Also incidentally fixes the later `app_dir in fixture_dirs` str-vs-Path comparison, making it a general rather than test-specific fix.

issues.description: str() works for str and Path, but os.fspath() is the more idiomatic coercion for path-like objects in Django/stdlib. Pure nit; behavior is identical for the relevant inputs.

summary: Patch correctly adds the missing self.save_m2m() call inside the commit branch, resolving the ManyToMany save bug exactly as ModelForm does; the hasattr guard is idiomatic and matches Django's own ModelForm.save pattern. Minimal, correct, no regression risk.

Correct, minimal fix: removes lossy to_native_string from the shared _encode_params (which mangled/failed on non-ASCII bytes bodies) and reinstates it only in the prepare_url path where native query strings are actually required. Matches the real upstream resolution; preserves binary body payloads while keeping URL param behavior intact.

issues.description: to_native_string conversion is now split between prepare_url and _encode_params; an inline comment explaining why URL params need native-string coercion but body data must pass through raw would aid future maintainers.

summary: Minimal, correct fix that replaces a hard `del` with `pop('to', None)` so the autodetector tolerates custom relation fields whose deconstruct() omits 'to'. Matches the reporter's suggestion and the actual Django fix; no regression or compatibility concern.

issues.description: pop('to', None) silently swallows the missing key rather than asserting on it, but since the only purpose was to make the field relation-agnostic, dropping a non-existent 'to' is harmless and the prior del was overly strict.

summary: One-line fix correctly replaces buggy apps.get_models(app_label) call (which ignored app_label and returned all project models) with apps.get_app_config(app_label).get_models(), matching Django's idiomatic API and resolving the reported issue.

Correctly fixes the dictionary-reuse bug by copying ms before each yield, fully resolving the issue with negligible performance cost. Only gap is the docstring still documents the old reuse caveat, which is a minor doc inconsistency.

issues.description: The docstring caveat warning that partitions() reuses/mutates the yielded dictionary is now stale and should be removed/updated, since each yield returns a fresh copy. Not merge-blocking but should accompany the behavior change.
ms.copy() adds a small per-yield allocation overhead, but this is an accepted and intended trade-off explicitly endorsed in the issue; negligible in practice.

summary: Minimal, correct fix for regex trailing-newline issue; replacing $ with \Z in both validators exactly resolves the reported quirk without regressions.

Replaces the buggy hand-rolled trim_docstring with stdlib inspect.cleandoc, which correctly handles non-empty first lines per PEP 257; this is the correct, minimal fix and matches Django's actual accepted patch. No correctness or regression problems block merge.

issues.description: Removes the trim_docstring helper from django.contrib.admindocs.utils. It is an undocumented internal utility, but third-party code importing it would break; acceptable for an internal admindocs helper but worth noting.
views.py already does 'import inspect', so the added 'from inspect import cleandoc' is redundant; could call inspect.cleandoc() instead of adding a second import. Pure style nit.
cleandoc does not per-line rstrip trailing whitespace as the old trim_docstring did; a negligible cosmetic difference for rST rendering, no functional impact.

summary: Removes the artificial multi-dim guard and replaces `mask.shape[axis]` with `np.take(mask.shape, axis).prod()`, correctly computing total reduced element count for both int and tuple axis. Minimal, correct fix matching the issue's suggested approach.

issues.description: `np.take(mask.shape, axis).prod()` works for int and tuple/list axis (np.take handles scalar and array indices incl. negatives), but relies on np.take coercing the shape tuple to an array; a direct `np.prod(np.take(...))` or comment would read slightly clearer. Not blocking.

summary: Correct, general fix for duplicate options from joined limit_choices_to: replaces complex_filter join with a correlated Exists(OuterRef('pk')) subquery using _base_manager, which is the standard Django approach to dedupe. No correctness, regression, or compatibility problems block merge.

issues.description: Guard changed from `if limit_choices_to is not None:` to `if limit_choices_to:`, so empty dict `{}` / empty `Q()` now skip filtering instead of applying a no-op filter. Behaviorally equivalent (empty filter was a no-op) but a subtle semantic shift worth noting.

Swaps a join-based filter for an Exists() correlated subquery; generally fine and the correct way to dedupe, but on some backends/queries the subquery form can have different performance characteristics than the prior join.

summary: Correct, minimal simplification of `_image()` that fixes the inverted-generator bug by mapping presentation symbols directly to domain generators and using signed powers from `array_form`. Approach is general (not test-specific), handles identity relators via empty `array_form`, and adds a helpful docstring.

issues.description: Correctness relies on `domain.presentation().generators` being in the same order as `domain.generators` for PermutationGroups (via `zip(symbols, domain.generators)`). This invariant holds in sympy's presentation() but is implicit; a brief comment would harden it against future changes.

summary: Adds a leading space to the Case template so COUNT(DISTINCT ...) no longer collides with CASE, correctly fixing the malformed SQL. The change is minimal and matches the existing SQL-assembly style in expressions.py.

issues.description: Leading space in the template is a slightly blunt fix (the extra space is harmless but relies on SQL whitespace tolerance rather than fixing joiner logic at the call site); acceptable and consistent with how other templates handle spacing in this file.

summary: Fix correctly replaces string-slicing with modulo arithmetic, matching Python strftime/PHP y-format semantics for years <1000; minimal, correct, no regressions found.

issues.description: Docstring style switched to triple-quotes while sibling methods (e.g. Y()) use single-quoted one-line docstrings, a small inconsistency but not merge-blocking.

summary: The patch makes SQLite's alter_field a noop whenever choices differ, but it short-circuits with OR, so an AlterField that changes choices AND a real schema attribute (max_length, null, etc.) in the same operation is silently skipped, leaving the column unaltered. Wrong layer and approach — the correct fix strips non-db attrs (choices, help_text, verbose_name, validators…) inside _field_should_be_altered, not a SQLite-only choices hack.

issues.description: Incorrect approach. `not _field_should_be_altered(...) or old_field.choices != new_field.choices` returns early on ANY choices delta. When choices change together with a genuinely db-affecting change (e.g. max_length, null, type) in one AlterField, the OR is True and the real alteration is dropped. Should be solved generically in `_field_should_be_altered` via Field.non_db_attrs.

Concrete regression: a single AlterField that modifies choices plus a real column attribute now produces no SQL on SQLite, causing schema drift versus the model state (and divergence from other backends).

Incomplete fix. Only `choices` is special-cased; other non-db-only attribute changes (help_text, verbose_name, validators, blank, error_messages, editable) still trigger a full table rebuild on SQLite, so the underlying problem class remains unresolved.
Overfit to the reported scenario (choices) rather than a general rule for schema-irrelevant attributes.
Fix lives only in the sqlite3 backend; the canonical Django solution centralizes attribute filtering in the base schema editor / Field metadata, keeping backends consistent.

summary: Adds a `return_ is not None` guard so constructors/functions hinted with `-> None` skip the unit conversion, correctly fixing the AttributeError. Minimal, targeted, behaviorally correct fix with no regression to existing return-annotation handling.

issues.description: Check keys on the returned value being None rather than the annotation being NoneType.
