A function annotated with a real unit that happens to return None would now silently skip conversion instead of erroring; acceptable edge case but slightly broader than checking `return_annotation is None`.
Second diff hunk re-adds `quantity_input = QuantityInput.as_decorator` identically (no-op whitespace/newline artifact); harmless but unnecessary.

summary: Adds 'joblib' to the dependency list reported by show_versions, directly resolving the issue. joblib is a core sklearn dependency, so listing it is correct, minimal, and consistent with the existing entries.
Minimal one-line fix correctly initializes `substitutions = False` before the loop, resolving the UnboundLocalError when max_post_process_passes=0 without altering normal-pass behavior.

Small, correct addition of refit_time_ attribute using a standard time.time() delta around the existing refit call, with docstrings updated for both GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV; no regression or compatibility risk.

issues.description: BaseSearchCV class docstring itself is not updated with refit_time_, only the two subclasses; minor documentation completeness gap.

summary: Moves the final e-step in fit_predict to after self._set_parameters(best_params), so log_resp is computed with the best initialization's parameters instead of the last init's — exactly fixing the fit_predict/predict disagreement when n_init>1. Correct, minimal, and idiomatic.
Converts method to builtin_str before .upper(), correctly fixing the Python 2 unicode method → UnicodeDecodeError bug at its source. Minimal, uses existing compat helper, no regression risk.

Correct, minimal fix that guards the `index < initial_form_count` comparison against `index is None`, resolving the TypeError raised by empty_form when can_delete=True and can_delete_extra=False. Matches the issue's proposed solution and Django's existing idiom.

Adds a final pass that strips all None-valued keys from the merged setting, correctly making `session.headers['X'] = None` suppress that header as documented. Fix is correct and general; only minor redundancy with the existing del-loop.

issues.description: New comprehension partially overlaps the existing `if v is None: del merged_setting[k]` loop, leaving two mechanisms doing similar work; the loop could now be subsumed, but leaving it is harmless.

summary: Minimal, correct fix that clamps the computed CPU count to at least 1 via max(1, ...), directly preventing the avail_cpu==0 crash in multiprocessing.Pool for both the cfs_quota and cpu.shares paths. No regression or compatibility concerns; matches the issue's suggested resolution.

issues.description: No comment explaining why the lower bound of 1 is enforced (i.e., to avoid the 0-CPU crash); a brief note would aid future readers, but the change is self-evident enough to merge without it.

summary: Adds an elif branch to CreateModel.reduce that folds a following AlterModelManagers into CreateModel, mirroring the existing AlterModelOptions optimization. Correct, minimal, idiomatic; resolves the issue cleanly.

issues.description: No inline comment, but matches surrounding style which also lacks comments; not a real gap.

summary: The patch relaxes the constraint-count guard from `!= 1` to `< 1`, which suppresses the crash but then unconditionally deletes only `constraint_names[0]` when multiple constraints match — and the introspection order is non-deterministic, so it may drop the unique_together's backing index instead of the intended index_together index. The correct, idiomatic fix is to make the lookup precise (pass `unique=False` in the `index` deletion path so exactly one constraint is found), keeping the strict guard intact.

issues.description: Wrong approach. When unique_together and index_together share columns, `_constraint_names(..., index=True)` returns 2 names (the _uniq backing index and the _idx). With `< 1`, the code falls through to `self.execute(self._delete_constraint_sql(sql, model, constraint_names[0]))` and deletes only the first. `_constraint_names` order is not deterministic, so this can delete the unique constraint's index rather than the index_together index. The accepted fix is to disambiguate the lookup (e.g. pass `{'index': True, 'unique': False}` to `_delete_composed_index` from `alter_index_together`) so exact

Behavioral regression / correctness risk: dropping the strict count check removes a useful safety net and can silently delete the wrong index. In the reported scenario the goal is to remove the index_together index while preserving the unique_together; deleting `constraint_names[0]` can instead remove the unique constraint's index, leaving the index_together in place and weakening the schema.

Incomplete: when more than one constraint matches, only one is ever deleted (the first), so the operation is neither a clean single-target delete nor a multi-delete. The fix should target precisely the index being removed rather than picking an arbitrary match.

summary: Correctly distinguishes a missing `__all__` (None → document implicit members) from an empty `__all__` (empty list → document nothing), which is exactly the reported bug. Minimal, well-commented, idiomatic change with no regression risk.
One-line fix replaces exhausting generator (StopIteration) with next(...,np.nan) fallback, matching expected 3.6.0 behavior for all-nan input; minimal and general, not test-specific.

issues.description: Returning np.nan works for numeric/datetime-like data but callers using non-numeric objects (e.g. custom unit types) may not handle a bare np.nan sentinel gracefully; edge case, not the reported bug.

summary: Adds 'joblib' to the dependency list in _get_deps_info, correctly resolving the issue since joblib became a hard dependency in sklearn >0.20. Minimal, well-placed, follows existing list convention.
Minimal one-line fix correctly extends InheritDocstrings to recognize property objects alongside functions, directly resolving the reported issue.

issues.description: Other descriptor types (e.g. classmethod, staticmethod, cached_property) still aren't handled, but that's outside the reported issue's scope.

summary: Fix correctly resolves the reported multi-line case by skipping the first line's zero indent, but omits the `default=0` guard, so `min()` now runs over an empty sequence for single-line docstrings and raises `ValueError: min() arg is an empty sequence`. This is a real regression on a very common docstring form.

issues.description: For a single-line docstring (e.g. `"""Test something."""`), `lines[1:]` is empty, so the generator yields nothing and `min(...)` raises `ValueError: min() arg is an empty sequence`. Previously this worked (indent=0). The correct fix needs `default=0`: `min((... for line in lines[1:] if line.lstrip()), default=0)`.
Incomplete fix: also crashes when all subsequent lines are blank/whitespace-only (empty filtered generator), same empty-sequence ValueError. Both cases collapse to the missing `default=0`.

summary: Adds __hash__ to ModelChoiceIteratorValue consistent with its __eq__, fixing the reported unhashable-type bug in a minimal, idiomatic way.

Correct minimal fix: the recursive branch for non-string (tuple/list) inputs dropped the `cls` argument, so nested names defaulted back to `Symbol`; passing `cls=cls` through propagates the intended class. Fully resolves the issue with no regression or compatibility risk.

Fix correctly mirrors AlterModelOptions.state_forwards() logic by clearing unset ALTER_OPTION_KEYS during CreateModel/AlterModelOptions squashing, resolving the reported bug with minimal, targeted change.

Minimal 2-line fix correctly extends set_output propagation to the remainder estimator, mirroring the existing per-transformer handling and resolving the reported dtype/column-loss bug for the common pre-fit set_output usage pattern.

issues.description: Only self.remainder (unfitted param) is updated; if set_output is called after fit, the already-fitted self.remainder_ clone used for future transform calls isn't touched. This mirrors an existing limitation for regular sub-transformers in the same method, so it's not a regression introduced by this PR.

summary: Simple, minimal setter mirroring the existing get_paths/_paths pattern used elsewhere in ContourSet; correctly resolves the enhancement request without altering existing behavior.

Minimal one-line fix: replacing identity check `in` with `issubclass()` correctly allows subclasses of BigAutoField/SmallAutoField/AutoField to satisfy AutoFieldMeta's subclass check, resolving the reported crash. Matches the suggested fix in the issue and is the same approach Django's real upstream patch used.

Minimal, symmetric fix: adds _legacy_encode() and routes encode() through it when DEFAULT_HASHING_ALGORITHM='sha1', mirroring existing _legacy_decode() fallback already used for decode(). Directly implements the fix proposed in the issue with no scope creep or regression risk to the default (non-sha1) path.

issues.description: Local variable `hash` shadows builtin, matching existing style in _legacy_decode but not ideal practice.

summary: Minimal, correct fix: sets self.pk = None after collector.delete() in Model.delete(), directly resolving the reported issue where deleting an instance with no dependent objects (fast-delete path) left the PK on the in-memory instance. Placement after collector.delete() ensures post_delete signal receivers still see the original pk, consistent with existing behavior for cascade-deleted related objects.

issues.description: Only clears pk on the instance calling delete(); does not affect other code paths (e.g. QuerySet.delete() or direct Collector.delete() use) which have their own separate pk-clearing logic, but that is outside the scope of this specific issue.

summary: Minimal, correct one-line regex fix that restricts URL userinfo characters to exclude ':', '@', '/' per RFC 1738, directly resolving the reported false-positive (e.g. http://foo/bar@example.com) without altering scheme, host, port, or path handling.

Correct, minimal fix: always casting xa to int (not only in the float branch) prevents the out-of-bounds uint8 assignment that triggered the NumPy 1.24 deprecation warnings, and also fixes a latent correctness bug where over/under/bad indices silently overflowed integer-dtype inputs. errstate is appropriately narrowed to wrap the NaN→int cast.

issues.description: np.errstate(invalid="ignore") now wraps only the astype cast; the added comment explains the cast (unsigned ints + floats) but not why errstate is still needed there (suppressing 'invalid value encountered in cast' for NaN floats). A one-line note would aid future readers.

Float-branch comparisons (xa < 0) and np.clip are no longer inside errstate. In practice these don't emit invalid warnings (minimum/maximum and quiet ops; suite/CI with warnings-as-errors passes on NaN colormap inputs), so no real regression, but the scope reduction is worth a glance.

summary: Fix correctly replaces ambiguous `in` (equality) sentinel check with `is` identity checks, resolving the numpy-array ValueError at its root rather than special-casing arrays; approach matches how mock's DEFAULT sentinel is meant to be compared.

issues.description: If `patchings` is set but neither 'mock' nor 'unittest.mock' is in sys.modules (previously an edge case returning len(patchings) via the `else` branch), the new code now returns 0 since both sentinel defaults become distinct dummy objects. This scenario is practically unreachable since patchings only appears via mock.patch decoration, so it's not merge-blocking.

summary: Patch adds an `index is not None` guard before comparing `index < initial_form_count`, exactly fixing the TypeError in empty_form/add_fields when can_delete and not can_delete_extra. Minimal, correct, general fix matching the issue's suggested resolution.

Minimal one-line fix correctly makes _eval_evalf recursively evalf function arguments before calling _imp_, resolving nested implemented-function evaluation exactly as described in the issue. Approach is idiomatic (mirrors how prec/dps is threaded elsewhere in this method), with fallback exception handling unchanged for non-numeric args.

Correctly resolves the transition issue by emitting legacy-format session data when DEFAULT_HASHING_ALGORITHM=='sha1', matching the existing _legacy_decode path so other instances during the 3.0→3.1 transition can decode it. Mergeable; only minor structural/comment nits.

issues.description: Legacy encoding is inlined in encode() rather than extracted to a _legacy_encode() helper symmetric with the existing _legacy_decode(); a small helper would read cleaner and mirror the decode side.

Missing a marker comment (e.g. RemovedInDjango40Warning) noting that the sha1 branch is temporary transition code tied to the deprecated DEFAULT_HASHING_ALGORITHM setting; the generic 'Use legacy encoding format' comment doesn't convey removal intent.

summary: One-line fix changes exact-membership check to issubclass(), correctly allowing user subclasses of BigAutoField/SmallAutoField to satisfy DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD's AutoField check. Minimal, general, matches the issue's suggested fix.

Cleanly moves use_required_attribute from ClearableFileInput up to FileInput so the required attribute is suppressed when initial data exists, exactly as the issue requests. Minimal, correct, idiomatic.

Refactors score_samples into a private _score_samples that skips input validation, and has fit() call it so feature names aren't stripped before computing offset_ via percentile. Correct, minimal, idiomatic fix that directly resolves the spurious warning.

issues.description: Order of check_is_fitted and _validate_data swapped in public score_samples: previously check_is_fitted ran first, now _validate_data(reset=False) runs first.
