issues.description: `sorted(expr.items())` compares SymPy Expr keys via `<`, which returns a Relational whose bool() raises TypeError. Any dict with 2+ non-trivially-comparable keys (e.g. Symbol keys) makes srepr crash. Should sort by a key function (e.g. default_sort_key / str) or not sort at all.
Regression: previously `srepr({x: y, a: b})` returned a string without error; now it raises TypeError. Behavior for multi-key dicts is worse than before the patch.
Fix only demonstrably works for the single-element dict in the issue; multi-element dicts (the general case) are unresolved/broken, so the issue is not fully fixed.

Sorting set on printed strings gives determinism but is inconsistent with list/tuple printers which preserve order; sorting choice for repr should follow sympy conventions (default_sort_key) rather than lexical string sort.

summary: Minimal one-line fix passes with_col_aliases=True to compiler.as_sql() for each combined query part, ensuring column aliases stay consistent across union/intersection/difference queries regardless of values()/values_list() re-evaluation. Matches the actual upstream Django fix for this issue and doesn't introduce new abstractions or scope creep.

Fix correctly skips auth.E003/W004 when USERNAME_FIELD has a UniqueConstraint, but the constraint check is too permissive: it accepts partial (conditional) and multi-field constraints that do not actually guarantee single-column uniqueness, allowing the error to be wrongly suppressed.

issues.description: Uses `cls.USERNAME_FIELD in constraint.fields`, so a multi-column UniqueConstraint (e.g. fields=['username','email']) wrongly silences E003 even though it does NOT enforce uniqueness of USERNAME_FIELD alone. Should require the constraint to cover exactly the single field (fields == (USERNAME_FIELD,) / len 1).

Does not check `constraint.condition is None`. Issue title explicitly says 'total UniqueConstraints'; a partial/conditional UniqueConstraint only enforces uniqueness over a subset of rows, so it must not satisfy the USERNAME_FIELD uniqueness requirement. Current code incorrectly accepts it.
Stray blank line added at top of file (line 1 before the itertools import) — unrelated whitespace, should be removed.

Relies on `models.UniqueConstraint` but the diff shows no `models` import in checks.py; if not already imported this raises NameError. Tests pass per premise, but reviewer should confirm the import exists.

summary: Patch special-cases `lookups[0] == 'in'` to collapse a MultiColSource into a single column, which resolves the reported subquery-column-count error but breaks legitimate multi-column relations. For composite/ForeignObject `__in` lookups that genuinely need all target columns, selecting only `targets[0]` yields incorrect filtering.

issues.description: Bypassing MultiColSource for all 'in' lookups is a fragile blanket rule. MultiColSource exists to compare every target column of multi-column foreign relations (ForeignObject/composite FKs); RelatedIn depends on receiving it to split the RHS across columns. Forcing a single `_get_col(targets[0])` silently drops the other join columns, producing wrong results for legitimate multi-column `__in` filters — a correctness break, not just the reported single-column case.

Regression risk for existing composite/multi-column relation filtering: any query relying on MultiColSource + 'in' now compares only the first target column instead of the full tuple. No guard distinguishes the reporter's reverse-m2m case from a genuine multi-column FK.

Fix keys on the exact `'in'` lookup string from the bug report rather than addressing the root cause (why the OR'd path selects all default columns for the related subquery). Reads as a targeted patch to the failing scenario rather than a general fix of the column-selection logic.
Hardcoded `'in'` magic string and terse comment; intent (why only 'in' is safe to collapse) is not explained for future maintainers.

summary: Patch correctly prevents roc_curve from emitting a first threshold >1 when scores are probability estimates by prepending 1 instead of thresholds[0]+1, resolving the reported issue without regressing the decision-function case (max>1 keeps old +1 behavior). Approach is slightly heuristic and lacks an explanatory comment, but is functionally sound and mergeable.

issues.description: Inferring 'this is a probability estimate' from thresholds.max() <= 1 is implicit/heuristic; a decision_function whose outputs happen to fall <=1 also takes this branch. Result is still a valid (0,0) sentinel point, so no correctness break, but the abstraction is a bit fragile compared to a sentinel like np.inf.
New conditional adds no comment explaining why the <=1 case prepends 1 (probability-clip rationale). A one-line comment would aid maintainability.
When thresholds[0] == 1 exactly, prepending 1 creates a duplicate leading threshold (non-strictly-decreasing). Harmless for curve semantics but slightly untidy.

summary: Fix makes comma-splitting bracket-aware so regexes with commas inside `(){}[]` (e.g. `(foo{1,3})`) survive parsing, resolving the reported crash. But it hand-rolls a fragile bracket counter and drops the whitespace-stripping that `_csv_transformer` previously applied, changing behavior for existing `a, b` style configs.

issues.description: Old path used `_csv_transformer`, which strips whitespace around each token. New per-char parser does NOT strip, so `bad-name-rgxs = foo, bar` now yields regex ` bar` with a literal leading space — silent behavioral regression for the common comma+space config style.

Manual bracket-depth counter is brittle: treats `()`, `[]`, `{}` interchangeably (mismatched pairs like `(a]` still balance to 0), ignores regex escaping (`\(` / `\)` are literals but still increment/decrement depth), and doesn't account for char-class semantics where `(`/`{` shouldn't count. Handles the reported case but not general regex grammar.
No comment explaining the bracket-tracking logic or why commas inside brackets are not split; non-obvious to future maintainers.

summary: The patch changes lookup_allowed()'s final relational check to match ANY prefix of relation_parts instead of the full relation path, which both fails to address the root cause (relation_parts still drops the 'place' hop for FK-as-PK during list-building) and dangerously loosens the DisallowedModelAdminLookup security guard. It edits the wrong location and introduces a permissive regression.

issues.description: Prefix matching over-permits: old code required the FULL relation path (join(relation_parts) or path+final part) to be in valid_lookups; new code returns True if ANY prefix matches. E.g. list_filter=['restaurant'] now allows lookup 'restaurant__place__country', weakening the DisallowedModelAdminLookup security check.

Wrong location for the fix. The reported bug is that relation_parts is built as ['restaurant','country'] because the FK-as-PK ('place') is treated as a target_field and skipped during the building loop. The root cause is the `field not in prev_field.path_infos[-1].target_fields` condition, not the final return; touching only the return cannot reinsert the missing 'place' hop.

Does not resolve the issue: with relation_parts still = ['restaurant','country'], the prefixes checked are 'restaurant' and 'restaurant__country', neither of which equals the valid lookup 'restaurant__place__country', so the DisallowedModelAdminLookup is still raised for the reported case.

summary: Removes the SimpleLazyObject wrapper that caused URL kwargs to remain unresolved lazy objects (crashing DB queries), returning plain values instead — correctly resolves the crash. Matches Django's actual resolution (un-deprecating URL-kwargs-in-context); only leftover cruft is the now-pointless closure.

issues.description: Leftover `def access_value(value=value): return value` then `context_kwargs[key] = access_value()` is a pointless closure; could be simplified to `context_kwargs[key] = value`. Harmless but unnecessary indirection.

Silently drops the RemovedInDjango40Warning deprecation notice for passing URL kwargs to context. This is intentional/aligned with the ticket's decision to un-deprecate, but worth noting the removed user-facing warning.

summary: Minimal correct fix that threads the already-parsed `evaluate` flag through to `cls(...)` in `Relational.__new__` and to `Relational.__new__` in `Unequality.__new__`, so `evaluate=False` is honored for relationals as the issue requires. Matches the expected `Lt(1,2,evaluate=False)` behavior and mirrors the sibling relational classes' construction path.

issues.description: Fix covers the general Relational.__new__ and Unequality paths, which is the right layer. Slight residual risk that other relational subclasses with their own __new__ bypass this path, but the two touched sites are the shared construction points so coverage is adequate.

summary: Fix correctly preserves the figure's original DPI across the FigureCanvasBase re-init during unpickling, addressing the M1 DPI-doubling root cause with a minimal 3-line change. Targeted, low-risk, and consistent with the surrounding __setstate__ code.

issues.description: Save/restore around FigureCanvasBase(self) is a bit of a workaround for the canvas re-init side effect rather than fixing the DPI mutation at its source, but it is a reasonable and safe pattern here.

summary: The patch emits `source-read` during `resolve_references` (post-parse/write phase) with `doctree.astext()` and discards the return value, so it does not modify any source or feed anything back into the doctree — the include'd content is never actually replaced. It also violates the event contract (handlers expect a mutable list `[text]`, not a bare string), which would crash real `source-read` handlers like the one in the bug report.

issues.description: Fundamentally wrong approach: emit result is thrown away and the call happens at reference-resolution time on an already-parsed doctree via astext(). Nothing modifies the doctree, so the actual bug (include'd source not passed through source-read at read time) is not fixed.

Issue not resolved. source-read must run on raw source before parsing so edits reach the parsed tree; here it runs after parsing and the emitted string is unused, so include'd content still is not replaced in output.

Contract break: source-read handlers receive a list and mutate source[0] in place. Passing a plain str (doctree.astext()) means handlers doing `source[0] = result` raise TypeError, breaking existing extensions such as the reporter's.

Emitting source-read a second time (at resolve time) for every document risks double-invoking handlers with side effects and is invoked once per resolve pass, causing unexpected behavior for existing extensions.

summary: Correctly extends PR #14047's simplified-path deconstruct technique to other public expressions (Func, Value, RawSQL, Star, Col, Window, WindowFrame, RowRange, ValueRange) via @deconstructible(path=...). Mechanical, consistent, low-risk change that produces cleaner migration output.

issues.description: Star and Col are internal-ish expressions not part of the public django.db.models namespace in the same way; asserting a path they may not resolve from could be slightly off, but this matches the existing pattern and is harmless for deconstruct output.

summary: One-line fix replaces `self.queryset.none()` with `self.queryset.model.objects.none()`, correctly returning an empty queryset for combined queries (union/intersection/difference) where `.none()` is a no-op. Matches Django's actual merged fix for this issue; minimal and correct.

issues.description: Root cause is that QuerySet.none() silently returns all rows on combined queries; patching the caller resolves the form symptom but the underlying QuerySet behavior remains. Acceptable and standard fix scope, but a maintainer may note it treats the symptom site rather than the query layer.

summary: Small patch adds classmethod-property handling in MethodDocumenter and PropertyDocumenter, and tests pass. However the PropertyDocumenter.can_document_member addition is logically redundant (its second disjunct is a subset of the existing inspect.isproperty check), signaling a confused/incomplete fix mechanism, plus formatting nits.

issues.description: In can_document_member, `inspect.isproperty(member) or (isinstance(member, property) and inspect.isclassmethod(member.fget))` is redundant: `isinstance(member, property)` already implies `inspect.isproperty(member)` (isproperty ends in `isinstance(obj, property)`), so the added disjunct is dead code and cannot be what actually enables documenting the member. Approach/mechanism is unclear and fragile.

Relies on `obj.fget`/`member.fget` being a classmethod, which matches `@property @classmethod` ordering; the reported bug is `@classmethod @property` (classmethod wrapping property). Whether the member Sphinx retrieves is actually a `property` instance with a classmethod fget is version/retrieval dependent (Python 3.9 returns the computed value), making correctness across the reported case questionable.
Trailing whitespace after `or` and awkward manual line continuation instead of parenthesized/black-style wrapping; inconsistent with repo formatting.
No comment explaining the non-obvious classmethod+property descriptor handling, which future maintainers will find cryptic.

summary: Adds Q.__rand__ mirroring __and__, making Q() & Exists(...) commutative with Exists(...) & Q(). Minimal, correct, matches Django's actual accepted fix for this ticket.

issues.description: Only __rand__ added; __ror__ not addressed. Issue text mentions '(and |)' but the reproduction and accepted fix scope only __and__/&. Not blocking since | works differently and was not part of the failing repro.

summary: Correctly extends HEAD-request fallback to retry with GET on TooManyRedirects, fixing infinite-redirect-loop URLs that regressed after HEAD was enforced in #7936. Change is minimal and correct; only nit is a redundant second edit.

issues.description: Second edit `except (Exception, requests.exceptions.TooManyRedirects)` is redundant: TooManyRedirects subclasses RequestException < Exception, so it is already caught by `Exception`. Harmless but adds noise; only the first except clause change is functionally needed.
First clause uses bare `HTTPError` (imported name) but new exception uses fully-qualified `requests.exceptions.TooManyRedirects`, mildly inconsistent import style.

summary: The patch replaces factorize's unique levels with `lev.astype(var.dtype)` (the full, non-deduplicated level index) rather than casting the factorized uniques. This works for the reported unique-coordinate case but silently corrupts values or raises for non-unique level coordinates, since `split_labels` (codes) index into deduplicated uniques while `levels` is now the full array.

issues.description: Uses `lev.astype(var.dtype)` (full original index) as the MultiIndex levels instead of the factorized uniques `lev.factorize()[1].astype(var.dtype)`. The codes from `factorize()[0]` index into the DEDUPLICATED uniques, but levels is now the full-length array, so code->value mapping is misaligned whenever a level coordinate has duplicate values. E.g. coord a=[0,0,1]: factorize codes=[0,0,1], patch levels=[0,0,1]; reconstruction gives [0,0,0] (wrong) or pd.MultiIndex raises 'Level values must be unique'. The correct dtype-preserving fix casts the factorized uniques, not the raw index.

Behavioral regression for stacking non-unique coordinate indexes: the original `lev.factorize()` produced correct unique levels; this change breaks that path (silent data corruption or ValueError), which the reproduction test does not cover.

Dense single-line comprehension zipping level_indexes with variables.values() is hard to read; splitting the dtype cast onto its own line (as the levels post-processing) would be clearer and less error-prone.

summary: The BoundField-based refactor of value access via `bf.value()` is correct, but collapsing the FileField isinstance branch into a single `bf.field.clean(value, bf.initial)` call passes a second positional arg to every field's clean(), which base `Field.clean(self, value)` does not accept (only FileField.clean takes initial). This raises TypeError for all non-FileField fields during validation.

issues.description: `bf.field.clean(value, bf.initial)` is called for ALL fields. Base `Field.clean(self, value)` accepts only one positional arg; only `FileField.clean(self, data, initial=None)` takes initial. Non-FileField fields (CharField, IntegerField, etc.) would raise `TypeError: clean() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`, breaking virtually all form validation. The original FileField isinstance guard must be retained.

Over-unification: the fix incorrectly assumes a uniform clean(value, initial) signature across all Field subclasses. Correct approach keeps the isinstance(field, FileField) branch and only passes initial to FileField.clean.

summary: One-line fix swaps `intersect` (returns unevaluated Intersection) for `intersection` (evaluates), so `is_subset` correctly compares the evaluated intersection to `self`. Minimal, targeted, resolves the reported wrong `is_subset` results without touching unrelated code.

issues.description: Fix relies on `intersection` producing an evaluated set equal to `self`; for set pairs where evaluation cannot simplify, `is_subset` may still return None (falls through). Acceptable since the method returns None as 'unknown' by design and the pre-existing XXX comment already flags this approach as suboptimal.

summary: Fix correctly resolves the stale-LEVEL_TAGS bug by resolving tags lazily per access instead of at import time, so @override_settings is honored. Main concern is removal of the module-level LEVEL_TAGS symbol (backward-compat) plus a stray blank line.

issues.description: Removes the module-level LEVEL_TAGS name. Third-party/internal code doing `from django.contrib.messages.storage.base import LEVEL_TAGS` breaks. The upstream-preferred approach keeps LEVEL_TAGS and refreshes it via the setting_changed signal, preserving the public symbol.
Adds a stray blank line as the new first line of the file — accidental, unrelated to the fix.
get_level_tags() recomputes tags on every level_tag access with no caching; the old module-level constant was computed once. Negligible in practice but avoidable.

summary: Change swaps hardcoded `keep_attrs=True` for `keep_attrs=keep_attrs` in `fillna` and `where_method`, making attr-preservation respect the resolved keep_attrs binding; repro + regression suites pass, confirming the reported attribute-dropping behavior is resolved without breaking existing behavior.

issues.description: Replacing hardcoded `keep_attrs=True` with `keep_attrs=keep_attrs` changes default behavior only if the resolved default differs from True; since the existing regression suite passes, prior attr-preservation is confirmed intact, so this is a note not a blocker.

`keep_attrs` is not declared in the shown function signatures nor bound by this diff, so correctness depends on an out-of-hunk binding (e.g. a parameter or `_get_keep_attrs()` default). Tests passing implies it resolves correctly, but the diff alone doesn't show its origin.

summary: Change tries to preserve input dtypes on pandas output but is fundamentally broken: it references an undefined `dtypes` variable in the default branch (NameError) and unconditionally forces output back to input dtypes, corrupting transformers that modify values. Not mergeable.

issues.description: In `_wrap_data_with_container`, the added `if dtypes is not None:` block references `dtypes`, which is never defined/assigned in that function scope. This raises `NameError` on the default (non-pandas) output path, breaking every estimator not configured for pandas output.

Unconditional `data_to_wrap.astype(dtypes)` using `original_input.dtypes` is a correctness regression for transformers that MODIFY values. E.g. StandardScaler/normalizers on an int column produce floats that get cast back to int (feature_names_out match original names), silently truncating/corrupting data. Dtype preservation must be opt-in and only when values are unchanged.

Feature is applied always rather than gated behind a config flag as the issue itself requested ('optionally preserve'). No mechanism to enable/disable; also fails when output columns differ from input (feature selection drops columns, transformers add columns) since dtypes is keyed by original column names.
New `dtypes` parameter of `_wrap_in_pandas_container` has no docstring entry describing it.
Stray blank line inserted at the very top of the file (before `from functools import wraps`); unrelated formatting noise.

summary: One-line indexing fix removes an extra trailing slice that caused an IndexError in the non-multinomial refit=False averaging path; matches the array's actual dimensionality and mirrors the analogous multinomial branch's approach.

The one-liner makes 'documented' call modify_field_list, which fixes the visible missing-return-type symptom but also makes 'documented' add :type:/:param: entries for UNDOCUMENTED parameters — collapsing the semantic distinction between 'documented' and 'all'. A maintainer aware of the config semantics would not merge as-is.

issues.description: 'documented' target semantic is 'only add type info for already-documented params/returns'. modify_field_list adds :type: and :param: fields for every annotation, including undocumented parameters, so this patch makes 'documented' behave identically to 'all' for param types. Reproduction case (all params documented) hides this because every field is documented, but users with partially-documented signatures now get types injected for undocumented params — a regression of the intended 'documented' behavior.

Wrong abstraction: correct fix should preserve documented-only param handling while still emitting the return type (e.g. augment path with rtype support / a suppress_rtype flag), not route 'documented' through the 'all' code path. Reusing modify_field_list is a shortcut that conflates two distinct config values.

summary: Passes `autodoc_type_aliases` into `typing.stringify` for both param and return annotations in the description-mode typehints path, exactly the missing plumbing that caused the bug. Minimal, correct, and consistent with how the signature path already resolves aliases.

Fix resolves the MultiOutputClassifier AttributeError, but discriminates meta-estimators via hasattr(estimator, 'estimators_'), which is too broad and mis-handles ensembles whose estimators_ are not per-label.

issues.description: Using `hasattr(estimator, 'estimators_')` as a proxy for MultiOutputClassifier is fragile. Many estimators expose `estimators_` where entries are NOT per-label sub-estimators (RandomForestClassifier/GradientBoosting/VotingClassifier/BaggingClassifier expose ensemble members). A more targeted check (isinstance MultiOutputClassifier / MetaEstimatorMixin, or presence of per-output classes_) would be safer.

Potential regression: RandomForestClassifier fit on multioutput y returns a list from predict_proba and previously worked via `estimator.classes_[i_label]` (a list of per-output class arrays). This patch now routes it through `estimator.estimators_[i_label].classes_`, indexing tree members as if they were labels, producing wrong class ordering/n_classes. cross_val_predict(method='predict_proba') on a bare multioutput forest could break.
The two branches duplicate the whole list comprehension differing only in the classes_ source; could be factored to compute the classes source once.

summary: Patch sets formfield.initial for UUIDField in formfield_for_dbfield, but this does not address the reported bug (the to_field target `id` is editable=False, so it never gets a formfield in the inline/admin form) and introduces a regression by assigning the NOT_PROVIDED sentinel as initial when a UUIDField has no default. Wrong layer and incorrect approach.

issues.description: Does not resolve the issue. The failing UUIDField (`id`) is `editable=False`, so `formfield_for_dbfield`/`formfield()` produces no editable form field for it; the real bug is that the parent's callable default is not populated before the inline FK (`to_field='id'`) is resolved on save. Setting formfield.initial here never fires for the reported scenario.

Wrong abstraction/fix location. The bug is in model save / related-field population for inlines with a `to_field` pointing at a defaulted field, not in admin form-field construction. Special-casing UUIDField in formfield_for_dbfield is a brittle, symptom-level patch.

Regression risk: when a UUIDField has no default, `db_field.default` is `models.NOT_PROVIDED` (not callable), so `formfield.initial = NOT_PROVIDED` — a sentinel leaks into the form as the initial value, altering rendering/behavior for editable UUIDFields without defaults. Guard should check `default is not NOT_PROVIDED`.

Fix is narrowly special-cased to UUIDField rather than the general class of fields with callable defaults used as FK to_field targets, indicating overfitting to the reported field type instead of a principled fix.
Comment says 'Ensure default values are set for UUIDField' but does not explain why UUIDField specifically or the interaction with editable=False / to_field, leaving intent unclear.

summary: One-line operand-order swap in Poly.__rmul__'s PolynomialError fallback so the Poly-derived expression is on the left of the multiply, making left-side `expr * Poly` evaluate like the right-side case. Minimal, correct, and matches the reported behavior; commutative multiplication makes the swap safe.

issues.description: No inline comment explaining that operand order (f.as_expr()*g vs g*f.as_expr()) is load-bearing for evaluation; a future cleanup could silently swap it back and reintroduce the bug.

summary: Patch fixes the reported symptom by nulling `.axes` on children during cla(), but the linked issue explicitly asks to unset BOTH `.axes` and `.figure`, and only `.axes` is handled. Core reported behavior is resolved; the `.figure` half of the request is left incomplete.

issues.description: Issue title/body request that cla()/clf() unset both `.axes` AND `.figure` of deparented artists (mirroring remove(), which nulls both). Patch only sets `artist.axes = None`, leaving `.figure` still pointing at the figure — the fix is partial versus the stated requirement.

Directly assigning `artist.axes = None` on all get_children() (which includes spines, xaxis, yaxis, patch, title that are reused/recreated by __clear) is slightly blunt; relies on subsequent __clear reassigning them. Works given passing tests but is a bit fragile.

summary: Patch merges consecutive same-multiplicity factors in dup_sqf_list so that all factors sharing a multiplicity collapse into the single square-free component s_i (e.g. (x-2)(x-3) → x^2-5x+6, mult 3), matching the square-free factorization definition and the reported expected output. Reasonable, minimal fix for the univariate dense path; main open question is whether the multivariate/dmp path needs the same treatment for full consistency.

issues.description: Fix only touches dup_sqf_list (univariate dense). If dmp_sqf_list / multivariate path can exhibit the same split-multiplicity output, consistency issue may persist there. Reported case is univariate, so acceptable, but worth confirming.

Merge collapses same-multiplicity entries at the output stage rather than addressing why the inner loop emits multiple partial factors for one multiplicity. Symptom-level fix, but since square-free s_i is exactly the product of those coprime pieces, the result is mathematically correct.
No inline comment explaining why same-multiplicity results are multiplied together; a one-line note would aid future maintainers.

summary: The change replaces a NotImplementedError with a ConditionSet return in _solve_trig, exactly matching the issue's requested behavior and consistent with how solveset signals unsolved equations elsewhere. Clean, minimal, correct fix; ConditionSet and Eq are already imported in the module.

issues.description: Callers that previously relied on _solve_trig raising NotImplementedError (to fall through to other solving strategies) now receive a ConditionSet instead. In practice solveset treats ConditionSet as the canonical 'unsolved' result, so this is the intended pattern and low risk, but worth a sanity check that no upstream caller branches on the exception.

summary: Patch inverts the result for the negated case: it sets sql='1=1' on EmptyResultSet but then falls through to the `if self.negated: sql='NOT {}'` wrapper, yielding 'NOT 1=1' (always FALSE) for `~Exists(none())` — the exact reported case, which should evaluate TRUE. This is a correctness bug that leaves the issue effectively unfixed (query still returns empty instead of the name='test' rows).

issues.description: Double negation. On EmptyResultSet with self.negated, sql is set to '1=1', but control then flows into the existing `if self.negated: sql = 'NOT {}'.format(sql)` block, producing 'NOT 1=1' = FALSE. `~Exists(none())` must be TRUE. Correct fix requires an early `return '1=1', []` (bypassing the NOT-wrap) or setting '0=1' pre-negation so it becomes 'NOT 0=1'=TRUE.

Because of the double negation, the reported scenario `filter(~Exists(none()), name='test')` still returns an empty QuerySet instead of rows matching name='test'. The bug is not actually resolved for the negated path.

Non-negated empty case returns '0=1' instead of re-raising EmptyResultSet. Functionally empty, but loses the EmptyResultSet short-circuit optimization Django relies on and diverges from the idiomatic handling; boolean literals '1=1'/'0=1' are also less portable than Value(True)/Value(False).

summary: Patch stops the IndexError but only by bounds-guarding the `del`, which masks the real defect: `blocks`/`num_blocks` shrink during iteration while `rep_blocks` does not, so index `i` desyncs across the three parallel lists. When the guard skips a delete, the non-minimal block system stays in `blocks`, so `minimal_blocks()` can silently return a non-minimal result instead of crashing.

issues.description: Root cause is index misalignment: `del num_blocks[i], blocks[i]` uses a `rep_blocks` index against lists that are being shortened in-loop while `rep_blocks` is filtered only afterward via `to_remove`. Guarding `i < len(...)` suppresses the crash symptom but does not realign the lists — with multiple non-minimal block systems the guarded-out entries remain in `blocks`/`num_blocks`, desyncing them from the filtered `rep_blocks`. A proper fix collects removal indices and deletes from all three lists consistently after the loop.

Because the skipped deletions leave stale non-minimal entries, the fix may not fully resolve the issue: it converts a hard IndexError into a potentially incorrect (non-minimal) return value for inputs that trigger more than one deletion, which is worse than crashing for a math library.
No comment explaining why the bounds guard is needed, leaving the subtle list-desync trap undocumented for future maintainers.

summary: Adds params={'value': value} to ValidationError calls across built-in validators, enabling %(value)s placeholder in custom messages as requested. Correct, minimal, consistent change that resolves the issue without regression.

issues.description: IPAddressValidator/other validators using RegexValidator inherit the fix, but some non-regex validators in the file (e.g. limit-value validators) are out of scope; acceptable given the issue focus on the listed validators.

summary: The one-liner adds `& finite` to the `even` rule so `even -> finite` now holds, fixing the reported case. But it only patches `even`; `odd` (defined symmetrically as `integer & !even`) is left unchanged, so `Symbol(odd=True).is_finite` is still None and the asymmetry lets an infinite integer be wrongly inferred as odd.

issues.description: Fix is asymmetric/incomplete: `odd == integer & !even` is untouched, so odd numbers still do NOT imply finite (Symbol('m', odd=True).is_finite == None). Same class of bug the issue reports, only half-fixed. Proper fix should also constrain odd (or add finite at the integer level).

Asymmetry introduces a wrong inference: for a symbol declared integer=True, finite=False, `even` becomes False (needs finite), then `odd == integer & !even` yields odd=True. So an 'infinite integer' is now incorrectly classified as odd, which was undetermined (None) before this change.

Change resolves exactly the reproduction case (even) without generalizing to the symmetric odd case, suggesting the patch is tailored to the reported example rather than the underlying 'integer should imply finite' principle.

summary: Minimal, targeted fix that wraps Literal annotation values in a `:const:` role instead of bare `repr()`, so nitpick no longer treats literal values (True, False, etc.) as py:class references. Correct and consistent across both restify and stringify code paths.

issues.description: Using `:const:` role for arbitrary Literal values (ints, strings, bools) is slightly semantically loose — `:const:` normally cross-references defined constants, not inline literal values. It works for suppressing the nitpick warning, but a plain-text/no-role rendering might be more precise. Not blocking.

summary: Fix flips the public default `check_rank=False` → `True` so `hermite_normal_form` no longer silently drops rows on rank-deficient input; a defensible correctness-over-speed default change, but the docstring still documents the old default and the change was not otherwise noted. Second diff hunk is a whitespace-only no-op.

issues.description: Docstring for `check_rank` still states `(default False)` / describes old opt-in semantics; flipping the actual default to True without updating the documented default leaves the docs inconsistent with behavior.

Public API default parameter value change: existing callers relying on the fast `check_rank=False` assume-full-rank path now get different behavior/cost by default. Backward-compatibility nuance worth a changelog note.
New default forces the rank-check code path (modulo-D branch) always, adding an avoidable rank computation for the common full-rank case.
Second diff hunk re-touches the final `return ... .to_Matrix()` line with an identical string (whitespace/newline no-op); unrelated churn.

summary: Correct, targeted fix that wraps a `None` return annotation in `:obj:`None`` so it renders as an intersphinx link in both signature and description modes, matching how autodoc handles other types. Resolves the reported inconsistency without regression risk.

issues.description: The 'None' → ':obj:`None`' conversion is duplicated in record_typehints and modify_field_list. Since record_typehints is the sole populator of annotations['return'], the check in modify_field_list is effectively defensive/redundant; a small helper or single conversion point would be cleaner.

Only bare 'None' is special-cased. Composite hints containing None (e.g. Optional[int] stringifying to 'Optional[int, None]'-style forms) are not linked, but that is outside the scope of this issue and consistent with how the rest of the module treats stringified annotations.

summary: Minimal, targeted fix that calls update_datalim on the step patch coordinates so density-scaled step histograms autoscale the y-axis correctly, matching the non-step histtype behavior. Correctly addresses the reported bug with no apparent regression risk.

issues.description: Comment '# Update data limits' is terse; a brief note on why step histtype needs explicit datalim update (patches don't auto-register extents) would aid maintainability, but acceptable.

update_datalim inside the per-dataset loop stacks column of (x,y) including baseline y=0; benign for typical cases but slight interaction possibility with log-scale/bottom offsets is untested — low risk, not blocking.

summary: Adds Max to known_functions mapping so mathematica_code renders it as valid Mathematica Max[...] syntax instead of the invalid Python-call-style output; minimal, targeted, low regression risk.

Correct, minimal swap to stdlib html.escape() that resolves the duplication/perf issue; the only behavioral change is ' encoded as ' instead of ', which is functionally equivalent HTML and was accepted upstream.

issues.description: Literal output for single-quote changes from ' to '. Functionally equivalent HTML but a backwards-incompatible textual change; should be noted in release notes, not merge-blocking.
The now-unused _html_escapes dict is left in place; docstring updated but dead mapping could be removed for cleanliness.

summary: Minimal one-line change to Figure.subfigures that forwards explicit margin args (left/bottom/right/top) to the GridSpec constructor, resolving wspace/hspace being ignored; reproduction and regression tests pass. Change is tightly scoped and low-risk.

issues.description: The added arguments pass the same values as GridSpec's defaults (None), so why this line is necessary to make wspace/hspace take effect is non-obvious. A short inline comment explaining the mechanism would help future maintainers and prevent someone from 'cleaning up' the seemingly redundant line.
Explicitly restating default None values reads as redundant at the call site; without context it looks like a no-op, hurting readability.

summary: Patch tries to make backward rename restore the old auto-generated name, but for an unnamed (old_fields) index self.old_name is None and the auto-generated name is never stored in state, so `get_index_by_name(self.old_name)` cannot recover it. Django's actual fix kept backward as a no-op for old_fields and instead made forward re-detect the current index by column via `_constraint_names`, making re-apply idempotent-safe; this approach is the wrong abstraction.

issues.description: For the unnamed/unique_together case (old_fields set), self.old_name is None, so `new_index = from_model_state.get_index_by_name(self.old_name)` calls get_index_by_name(None), which raises 'No index named None'. The auto-generated old index name is not stored in ModelState.options['indexes'] (only the forward-added Index named self.new_name is), so the target name simply cannot be reconstructed from state this way. Correct approach detects the DB index by columns via schema_editor._constraint_names, as done in the forward path.

Because the target (old auto-generated) name is unrecoverable from state, the backward operation cannot actually rename the index back for the exact reported scenario (unnamed index for unique_together), so the crash-on-re-apply bug is not correctly resolved. The forward path is left untouched, so idempotency of re-apply is not addressed at its real source.

Renaming inside database_backwards for old_fields diverges from Django's chosen design (backward = no-op, forward re-detects by column). Even if it happened to satisfy a narrow test, it is special-cased rather than a general, column-based fix.

summary: Two-line fix makes len() of rank-0 arrays return 1, matching numpy semantics and the iterator's element count. Minimal, correct, no regression risk for higher-rank arrays.

issues.description: Special-casing shape==() in __len__ patches the symptom rather than fixing _loop_size at construction; a cleaner fix would set _loop_size=1 for rank-0 so all consumers agree. Acceptable as-is.

summary: The patch only guards `_aggregate_score_dicts` against an empty score list, masking the IndexError symptom rather than fixing the root cause: the generator passed as `cv` is exhausted after the first `cross_val_score` call inside SequentialFeatureSelector's candidate loop. It prevents the crash but leaves SFS scoring most feature candidates against an empty CV, silently producing nan/arbitrary selections.

issues.description: Wrong layer of fix. Real bug is generator/iterable-of-splits exhaustion: check_cv/_CVIterableWrapper materializes the generator on the first cross_val_score call, so every later call in SFS's loop gets an empty split set. Correct fix is to materialize splits to a list once in SequentialFeatureSelector (or upstream), not to special-case empty results in the shared low-level aggregation utility.

Fix is incomplete/incorrect end-to-end. With the generator consumed, all feature candidates after the first evaluation receive an empty CV, yielding empty/nan scores. Returning `{}` stops the exception but SFS then selects features from meaningless scores — the documented 'pass an iterable of splits' behavior still does not actually work correctly.

Returning `{}` from `_aggregate_score_dicts` for empty input can propagate an empty dict into cross_validate result assembly (e.g. results['fit_time']), risking KeyError or malformed outputs on other empty-CV paths that previously failed loudly; masking the empty case in a widely-used helper changes failure semantics silently.

summary: The center-handling logic is incorrect and fragile: because `starts[:window]=0` is applied before subtracting `offset`, the first windows get negative start indices that rely on Python's negative-index slice emptiness, and the label-reassignment produces duplicated left labels while silently dropping the right-edge windows, so manual iteration still does not reproduce `rolling(center=True).mean()`.

issues.description: Label reassignment `label = self.window_labels[start+offset]` duplicates the first label multiple times and never yields the rightmost windows/labels. For the issue's own example (n=9, w=3) the last valid centered value (8.0) is never produced and label[0] is emitted 3x, so the (label, window) sequence does not match the centered .mean() output the issue asks for. Fix is incomplete/incorrect.

`starts = starts - offset` runs AFTER `starts[:window]=0` clamps, giving negative starts (e.g. -1). `obj.isel(slice(-1,1))` uses Python negative-index semantics and returns an empty window rather than a clipped left-edge partial window. Correctness accidentally depends on emptiness + min_periods masking; with different min_periods it would yield wrong data. Should clip starts/stops to [0, n], not shift blindly.

Changes the (label, window) pairing and per-label window contents of an existing public iteration protocol; because right-edge windows are dropped and labels duplicated, code relying on manual DataArrayRolling iteration with center=True gets a different/incorrect sequence.
The inline ternary relabel and the double `if self.center[0]` checks are unclear and uncommented; intent (offset windows then relabel to centered position) is not documented.

summary: Patch adds samesite to delete_cookie's set_cookie call, resolving reported issue that deleted cookies lost SameSite/Secure semantics; matches Django's actual accepted approach for this ticket.

issues.description: delete_cookie() has no samesite parameter of its own, so it always uses SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE regardless of what samesite value the cookie being deleted originally had (e.g., cookies unrelated to sessions, like CSRF or custom app cookies with a different SameSite policy).

Tying delete_cookie's samesite for any cookie to the SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE setting is a naming/semantic stretch since delete_cookie is a general-purpose method, not session-specific, though this matches the documented tradeoff Django accepted for this fix.

summary: The patch adds a MatrixSymbol-only special case to _print_Add, but a bare MatrixSymbol always has coefficient +1, so the new branch never emits a '-' and produces identical output to the old code; the actual negative terms in the issue (`-A*B`, `-B`) are MatMul objects, not MatrixSymbol, so they are not handled at all. The approach cannot resolve the reported bug and is likely non-functional (also risks a NameError if MatrixSymbol is not imported in str.py).

issues.description: Only `isinstance(term, MatrixSymbol)` is special-cased, but the problematic terms `(-1)*A*B` and `(-1)*B` are MatMul, not MatrixSymbol. Those negative-product terms fall through to the else branch and still print as `(-1)*A*B` / `(-1)*B`, so the reported issue (differences of matrix expressions) is not actually fixed.

A bare MatrixSymbol's `as_coeff_Mul()[0]` is always +1, so `< 0` is never true and `t = self._print(as_coeff_Mul()[1])` reprints the same symbol. The new branch is effectively a no-op — wrong abstraction; a correct fix needs coefficient handling on MatMul or a dedicated `_print_MatAdd`.

The diff references `MatrixSymbol` with no import added (only +4 lines shown). If str.py does not already import MatrixSymbol at module scope, `isinstance(term, MatrixSymbol)` raises NameError on every Add print — a broad regression. Import must be verified/added.
`as_coeff_Mul()` is called twice for the same term instead of unpacking once; minor style/efficiency inconsistency with the surrounding code.

summary: The patch tries to undo newline translation after the fact via blind string replacement instead of preventing the translation at the source (open the capture buffer with newline=""). This unconditionally rewrites every '\n' to '\r\n', corrupting genuine newlines in all captured output — a broad regression and a fragile, incorrect approach.

issues.description: Wrong abstraction: once the text buffer has translated line endings, original '\r' vs '\n' vs '\r\n' are indistinguishable, so a post-hoc replace cannot faithfully reconstruct input. Correct fix is to disable universal-newline translation on the capture file (newline=""), not reverse-engineer it.

res.replace('
','
') turns EVERY genuine newline in captured stdout/stderr into '
' (the '
'->'' pass only covers a narrow case). Any existing test comparing captured output against '
'-terminated strings would now see '
' — real behavioral regression across the whole capture surface.
Heuristic is shaped to make the '\r'-ending reproducer pass rather than to solve newline handling generally; behavior on mixed/interleaved '\r' and '\n' is unspecified and likely wrong.
Single-quoted string literals inconsistent with pytest's black/double-quote convention.

summary: Correct, minimal fix that generalizes the distributive-reduction path so Mod applied to individual Mul factors (e.g. Mod(3*i,2) -> Mod(i,2)) triggers restructuring even without a pre-existing inner Mod. Approach is sound, matches upstream intent, no clear regression.

issues.description: Dropped the explanatory '# finding distributive term' comment; the new `was`/`changed` logic would benefit from a one-line note on why non_mod_l is always recomputed and compared.

non_mod_l = [cls(x, q) ...] is now computed unconditionally (previously only when inner Mods present), adding a small recursive-eval cost on the common path, though the result is reused so impact is negligible.

summary: Change serializes Enum by .name instead of .value, matching Django's actual accepted fix for this issue; it correctly makes migrations stable under translated/mutable enum values. Approach is sound and minimal.

issues.description: Edge case: enum members that are aliases (duplicate values) or Enums whose name differs semantically are handled fine by name lookup, but Flags/IntFlag combined values (e.g. FlagA|FlagB) have no single .name and would serialize to None — a rare corner not covered here, later addressed by a separate EnumSerializer path.

summary: Patch special-cases IndexVariables in Dataset.copy to skip the copy that casts '<U*' to object, but it only touches dataset.py while the issue also reports DataArray.copy (ds.z.copy) casting unicode indices — that path lives in dataarray.py and copies coords via v.copy(deep=deep) directly, so it remains broken. Sharing the original IndexVariable object also skips genuine copying (attrs/encoding aliasing) rather than fixing the root cause in IndexVariable.copy.

issues.description: Issue explicitly covers DataArray.copy(deep=True/False) (In[6]/In[7]), but DataArray.copy has its own path copying self._coords with v.copy(deep=deep) and does not route through Dataset.copy. This one-line edit in dataset.py leaves the DataArray case unfixed — incomplete resolution.

Root cause is IndexVariable.copy(deep=True) casting '<U*' to object; correct fix belongs there so all callers benefit. Bypassing the copy entirely returns the SAME IndexVariable object into the copied Dataset, so mutable attrs/encoding become aliased between original and 'deep' copy — a subtle regression versus true copy semantics.
Special-casing at the call site rather than fixing IndexVariable.copy reads as narrowly patched to the failing Dataset path instead of a general fix.

summary: Minimal one-line fix correctly adds a 'public' metadata override to the isprivate exclusion branch, directly resolving the reported issue without altering unrelated logic.

issues.description: Parentheses around 'isprivate and ...' are redundant given 'and' precedence, but harmless.

summary: The patch does not fix the reported bug and is logically inverted: it adds a condition to OMIT storage when the callable returns default_storage, whereas the issue requires the callable reference to always be INCLUDED. It also re-invokes the callable during deconstruct, introducing non-determinism and side effects.

issues.description: Does not resolve the issue. In the exact reported case (callable evaluates to default_storage), self.storage IS default_storage, so `self.storage is not default_storage` is already False and short-circuits — storage is still omitted. The added clause never runs in that case, so the bug persists. Correct fix (per Django's actual resolution) is to compare the _storage_callable reference against default_storage: `storage = getattr(self,'_storage_callable',self.storage); if storage is not default_storage: kwargs['storage']=storage`, which always includes a callable reference.

Inverted/incorrect logic and fragile approach. The new clause suppresses the storage kwarg precisely when the callable returns default_storage — the opposite of the issue's requirement that the callable be deconstructed as a reference. Worse, it calls `self._storage_callable()` a second time at deconstruct; for the example callable (random.choice) this is non-deterministic with side effects and can yield a different result than __init__, producing unstable migrations.

Behavioral regression: re-invoking the storage callable during deconstruct violates the design where the callable is evaluated once in __init__. Any callable with side effects or randomness now runs again unexpectedly during makemigrations.

summary: Patch adds a hardcoded non-standard `Proxy-Connection: keep-alive` header inside `HTTPProxyAuth.__call__`, but the reported bug uses `proxies=` dict where proxy auth flows through `rebuild_proxies`/`proxy_headers`, not `HTTPProxyAuth`, so this code path is not even exercised by the repro. Wrong location, non-standard header, and unconditional injection make it a fragile, likely non-fixing change.

issues.description: `HTTPProxyAuth` is a manual auth class; the reported scenario (`requests.get(url, proxies=proxies)`) sets `Proxy-Authorization` via `rebuild_proxies`/`HTTPAdapter.proxy_headers`, not through `HTTPProxyAuth.__call__`. The edited path is not on the default proxy flow, so the change likely does not resolve the actual 407 for the reported use case.

Root cause is the CPython 3.8.12 backport affecting tunneled HTTPS proxy connections at the urllib3/http.client layer. Injecting a header only when a user explicitly opts into `HTTPProxyAuth` leaves the common `proxies=` path (the one in the report) unfixed.
`Proxy-Connection` is a non-standard/deprecated hop-by-hop header; hardcoding `keep-alive` unconditionally is brittle and may conflict with connection handling for proxies that don't expect it.
Appears special-cased to satisfy a repro that directly invokes `HTTPProxyAuth`, rather than fixing the general proxy-auth path that the issue describes.

summary: The added `if M.shape[i] > 0:` guards are functionally a no-op: `for i in range(0)` already iterates zero times, so wrapping the loops changes nothing and does not alter the computed shape. The change neither fixes the reported dense Matrix.hstack/vstack shape bug (which lives in the matrix join code, not BlockMatrix.shape) nor prevents any IndexError, since the guards sit on the wrong dimension relative to the indexing `M[i,0]`/`M[0,i]`.

issues.description: Guards are ineffective. `if M.shape[0] > 0:` around `for i in range(M.shape[0]):` is redundant because range(0) is already empty; identical output for every input, including empty/zero-size blocks. Change has no behavioral effect.

Reported issue is Matrix.hstack/vstack (dense Matrix) returning (0,3) instead of (0,6). That path does not go through BlockMatrix.shape; root cause is in the row_join/col_join reduce logic. This diff cannot resolve the linked issue.
Even if intended defensively, guarding a loop that is already safe against zero-length ranges adds noise and misleads future readers into thinking an edge case is handled.

summary: Small, targeted fix that maps min-similarity-lines=0 to float('inf') so no code block can ever meet the duplicate threshold, disabling the check as requested. Works and is commented, though float('inf') is a slightly hacky sentinel for an int-typed setting.

issues.description: Using float('inf') as sentinel for an int-typed line count is a bit fragile; downstream code that does integer arithmetic with min_lines (e.g. range(len - min_lines)) could raise TypeError if it isn't already guarded. Tests pass so current paths are safe, but an explicit disable flag/early-return would be cleaner.
Inline comment present, but user-facing docs for min-similarity-lines aren't updated to mention that 0 disables the check.

summary: Small, targeted change in admin get_search_results that builds the per-term OR filter via an explicit Q() |= loop instead of the positional-tuple Q(*generator, _connector=OR) form, which is the join-reusing pattern needed to avoid the extra joins reported in the issue. Functionally correct (empty Q() is the OR-identity in Django, so the loop is equivalent to reduce(or_)) and passes the reproduction and regression suites.

issues.description: Replacing a single Q(...) expression with a mutable Q() plus in-place |= loop is slightly more verbose; a reduce(operator.or_, ...) or comprehension could express the same intent more idiomatically, but this form is clear and matches long-standing Django admin style.

No inline comment explaining that the loop form is intentional (join reuse / avoiding unnecessary JOINs); a one-line note would prevent a future refactor from reintroducing the generator/_connector form. Not merge-blocking.

summary: Adds `valid_ordering_lookups = {'isnull'}` to Options, matching Django's actual accepted approach for allowing the isnull lookup in ordering (ticket #30293). Correct minimal fix; only concern is the narrow whitelist, which is intentional scope.

issues.description: Only 'isnull' is whitelisted. Other boolean-producing lookups usable in order_by still raise E015. Acceptable/intended scope (isnull is the common orderable lookup) but not a fully general lookup-vs-transform fix.
New attribute introduced with no inline comment explaining why only 'isnull' is permitted in ordering; a one-line comment would aid maintainability.

summary: Patch resolves the reported `__in` + alias/annotate case by clearing the select clause, but it does so unconditionally for every query compiled through `Query.as_sql` (i.e. all subqueries), not just the `__in` RHS. Clearing column selection this broadly—and as a mutating side effect inside `as_sql`—is an unsafe generalization that a Django maintainer would want scoped to the lookup path.

issues.description: Fix is placed in the wrong/too-broad location. `Query.as_sql` (with only the `self.subquery` guard) runs for EVERY query used as a subquery expression — `Subquery()`, correlated subqueries, nested subqueries — not just the `__in` RHS. `clear_select_clause()` wipes `self.select`, `default_cols`, and the annotation mask, so any subquery whose selected columns are not re-specified via `values()` is at risk of selecting the wrong columns. The correct fix belongs in the `__in`/RelatedIn RHS handling, not in generic subquery compilation.

Behavioral regression risk: mutating the query (clearing select) as a side effect during `as_sql` compilation is fragile — it permanently alters the query object at SQL-generation time, which can surprise re-compilation, cloning, or reuse of the same query, and broadens column-selection semantics for all subqueries beyond the narrow bug.

Comment 'Ensure only necessary columns are selected in subqueries' is vague and does not explain WHY (annotate/alias leaking columns into an `__in` RHS) or why the broad `self.subquery` guard is safe.

summary: Wraps converter loop in try/except ValueError to return NotImplemented, letting reflected operators (__radd__) engage per numpy subclassing convention. Correct, minimal fix matching the issue and numpy docs.

issues.description: `except ValueError` is broad — could swallow a legitimate ValueError from _condition_arg (e.g. genuinely un-convertible value) and turn it into NotImplemented, surfacing later as a less informative TypeError instead of the original message. Scope is narrow in practice (unit incompatibility handled earlier via converters), so low risk, but a tighter catch or comment noting intent would be cleaner.
No inline comment explaining why ValueError maps to NotImplemented (deferring to reflected operators). Aids future maintainers but not merge-blocking.

summary: Small targeted fix: converts fk_value to str before get_prep_value when the related model's pk is a UUIDField, resolving the GFK+UUID prefetch mismatch. Change is minimal, low-risk, and doesn't alter behavior for non-UUID pk types.

issues.description: Hardcodes an isinstance check against models.UUIDField rather than a more general normalization strategy; works for the reported case but is a narrow special-case rather than a broadly generalized fix for other custom pk field types with similar str/native mismatches.

summary: The warning text says structured arrays will become Columns 'in future versions,' but the code already changes the behavior to Column(data) immediately — a self-contradicting, premature breaking change that ignores the issue's explicit two-stage plan (warn now, change in 5.2).

issues.description: Behavior is changed NOW: structured ndarray becomes a Column (data_is_mixin=False) instead of NdarrayMixin. This is an immediate backward-compat break for anyone relying on NdarrayMixin behavior (serialization signaling, .info handling), landing without the deprecation period the FutureWarning promises.

Contradicts the linked issue's design: proposal was to add a FutureWarning while KEEPING NdarrayMixin behavior for this release, then remove the clause in 5.2. Diff does both at once, so the migration warning is meaningless — the change it warns about has already happened.

Warning message 'In future versions, structured ndarray will be added as a Column' is misleading/false given the code adds it as a Column in this very version; message and behavior disagree, confusing users who cannot avoid the (already-applied) change by wrapping in Column.

summary: The patch is logically a no-op: `hasattr(expression, 'filterable') and not expression.filterable` is semantically identical to the original `not getattr(expression, 'filterable', True)` for the reported case (a model instance whose `filterable` field is False), so it still raises NotSupportedError and does not fix the bug. The correct fix must restrict the check to actual expressions (e.g. gate on `hasattr(expression, 'resolve_expression')`), not on the presence of a `filterable` attribute.

issues.description: Wrong approach. For a model instance with field filterable=False, hasattr(expression,'filterable') is True and not expression.filterable is True -> still raises. This is equivalent to the original getattr(...,True) branch, so it fails to distinguish a real expression from a model instance that merely happens to have a 'filterable' attribute. The root cause (check_filterable applied to non-expression values) is untouched.

Issue not resolved. The reported filter ProductMetaData.objects.filter(metadata_type=<instance with filterable=False>) still hits the raise branch, so NotSupportedError is not prevented. Proper fix gates on an expression marker like resolve_expression.

summary: Fix correctly copies xy/xytext arrays before storing in Annotation, resolving mutable-reference bug from the report with minimal, correct scope.

issues.description: Resulting line exceeds project's typical line-length convention (~79 cols) and crams a ternary inline, slightly hurting readability/PEP8 compliance.
Inline conditional np.copy(xytext) if xytext is not None else None could be simplified to a small helper or pre-computed variable for clarity.

summary: Patch sympifies string p (and string q) before the numeric path, correctly fixing Rational('0.5','100') → 1/200 by reusing existing SymPy parsing. Sound, minimal, low-risk; only edge-case asymmetry and a comment nit.

issues.description: Only converts q when p is also a str. Cases like Rational(0.5, '100') (float p, str q) are not routed through sympify, so string-q handling stays inconsistent. Not the reported case, but leaves a related edge unaddressed.
Catching SyntaxError alongside SympifyError and silently passing ('error will raise below') is slightly fragile; relies on downstream to re-raise a meaningful error rather than validating here.
New string-coercion block adds a special-case branch at the top of __new__ with no docstring/example note; a brief comment on why strings need pre-sympification would aid maintainability.

summary: The diff swaps `nargs="*"` for `nargs=argparse.REMAINDER` in dbshell.py, but the reported bug (extra parameters placed AFTER the dbname in the psql command) is caused by argument ordering in the PostgreSQL backend client (settings_to_cmd_args_env), not by how dbshell collects parameters. This change does not move parameters before the database name and therefore does not resolve the issue.

issues.description: Issue asks that extra parameters precede the dbname on PostgreSQL. That ordering is built in django/db/backends/postgresql/client.py, which is untouched. Changing nargs in dbshell.py cannot reorder parameters relative to dbname, so psql still ignores '-c ...'. Fix is in the wrong file.

Wrong abstraction/approach: parameter collection (nargs) is orthogonal to the argv ordering that psql requires. Both nargs="*" and REMAINDER capture the params after '--'; the defect is placement in the backend command builder.

Potential NameError: dbshell.py does not import argparse. If argparse is not imported in the module, `argparse.REMAINDER` raises at runtime. (Assumed importable given tests pass, but must be verified.)
Second hunk is a no-op trailing-whitespace/newline touch on the closing `)` — unrelated cosmetic churn.

summary: Patch adds ensure_ascii=False to json.dumps(not self.is_required) in AutocompleteMixin, but that argument is a boolean whose serialization never contains non-ASCII characters, so the change has zero effect on the reported JSONField unicode display bug. Wrong location entirely — real fix belongs in JSONField.prepare_value (django/forms/fields.py), not the admin autocomplete widget.

issues.description: Issue not resolved. Bug is about JSONField admin display escaping unicode (e.g. 中国 -> \u4e2d\u56fd). Patch touches AutocompleteMixin's data-allow-clear which serializes a bool (not self.is_required); json.dumps(True/False) yields 'true'/'false' — no unicode ever. Real JSONField widget/prepare_value path untouched.

Incorrect approach/wrong location. ensure_ascii=False on boolean serialization is meaningless. Correct fix is in django/forms/fields.py JSONField.prepare_value (or the field's bound_data), where actual JSON string values are dumped.
Change looks special-cased to pass a repro test that only checks the string 'ensure_ascii=False' appears, rather than actually correcting unicode handling in JSONFields.

summary: Minimal, correct fix mirroring the existing make_hashable(limit_choices_to) pattern already used in this class; resolves the exact TypeError from the issue.

The patch fixes the crash by quoting table names, correctly resolving the reserved-word failure, but it hardcodes MySQL-style backticks instead of using Django's standard SQLite identifier quoting (quote_name / double quotes). It works functionally since SQLite accepts backticks, but is inconsistent with repo convention.

issues.description: Hardcoded backticks (`) for identifier quoting mismatch Django's SQLite convention. Elsewhere Django uses self.ops.quote_name(...) which emits double-quoted identifiers (SQL standard). Backticks are a MySQL-ism SQLite tolerates but idiomatic fix would call quote_name(table_name).

Column identifiers in the SELECT (primary_key_column_name, column_name) remain unquoted; a reserved-word column name would still fail. Out of the reported scope (table names) but the same class of bug is left partially unaddressed.
String-formatting identifiers via %s is fragile; relying on quote_name would be safer and self-documenting versus manually wrapping in literal backtick characters.

summary: The patch modifies `post_mortem` in debugging.py to use `sys.exit` instead of `outcomes.exit`, which is entirely unrelated to the linked issue (interpreter crash on debug builds from `Expression.compile("False")` in the mark expression evaluator). It fixes nothing in the reported bug and replaces pytest's controlled exit mechanism with a raw SystemExit.

issues.description: Does not resolve the reported bug. Issue is a CPython assertion crash when the mark expression compiler compiles reserved names True/False/None as name loads (src/_pytest/mark/expression.py). Change touches debugging.py and leaves the actual crash unaddressed.
Wrong file/wrong abstraction entirely; edit has no causal connection to the linked issue's reproducer.

Replacing outcomes.exit (raises pytest's Exit/Session control exception) with sys.exit (raw SystemExit) bypasses pytest's controlled shutdown path, a likely behavioral regression in debugger-quit handling.
Inline `import sys` inside the function and use of sys.exit instead of the established outcomes.exit idiom conflict with repo conventions.

summary: Minimal, idiomatic __getstate__/__setstate__ that mirrors matplotlib's established pickling pattern (same as Figure/other artists) and resolves the unpicklable-canvas chain through the draggable legend. Correct approach, matches repo conventions, no regression or compatibility break.

issues.description: After unpickling, self.legend is permanently None, so the DraggableLegend loses its back-reference and drag behavior is not restored (user must call set_draggable again). Acceptable known limitation for pickle support, not a merge blocker.

Comment 'Remove the unpicklable entries' is slightly imprecise — it nulls the legend reference to break the path to the unpicklable canvas rather than removing an inherently unpicklable object; a one-line note on why would aid future readers.

summary: Adds violation_error_code plumbing to BaseConstraint and forwards it to the ValidationError raise sites, which resolves the core request. But it omits updating deconstruct() and __eq__, so the new attribute is lost in migration serialization and two constraints differing only by code compare equal.

issues.description: deconstruct() is not updated to include violation_error_code, so the attribute is dropped from migration serialization; constraints reload without the custom code. Incomplete fix for a persisted field.
__eq__ not updated, so two constraints identical except for violation_error_code compare equal — breaks equality/change-detection semantics and can mask migration state changes.
self.violation_error_code = violation_error_code is assigned twice (top of __init__ and again lower). Redundant duplicate write.
The '# RemovedInDjango60Warning.' comment marking the deprecation block was replaced by the assignment, losing that marker; docstring/attribute documentation for the new param also not added.

summary: The quantile fix itself is correct and resolves the issue, but the diff also silently modifies sortby, which has no `keep_attrs` parameter in its signature — referencing `keep_attrs` there raises NameError on every sortby call. That is an unrelated, broken change that would break existing behavior.

issues.description: The sortby edit references a `keep_attrs` name that is not a parameter of DataArray.sortby (its signature is `sortby(self, variables, ascending=True)`). Any call to sortby now hits `if keep_attrs:` on an undefined name -> NameError, breaking previously working, untested behavior.

Scope creep: the issue is strictly about quantile honoring keep_attrs, but the patch also modifies sortby (which the bug report never mentions and which does not even expose keep_attrs). This unrelated edit is what introduces the regression above.

In quantile, keep_attrs is already forwarded to ds.quantile(...) and then attrs are re-applied on the DataArray wrapper; the manual re-assignment is a defensible belt-and-suspenders but slightly redundant/fragile if the underlying Dataset path is later fixed.

summary: The patch adds a defensive `iscoroutine` check in `get_response_async`, but this runs AFTER the outermost (first) middleware has already executed its `process_response`, so it does not stop that middleware from receiving a coroutine — the actual reported symptom. It fixes the wrong layer (boundary return value) instead of the root cause in `MiddlewareMixin`, which must await its async inner `get_response` before invoking `process_response`.

issues.description: Reported bug is that the first middleware's process_response() receives a coroutine. That call happens INSIDE _middleware_chain execution (the outermost middleware), before control returns to get_response_async. Conditionally awaiting the chain's return value cannot retroactively change what process_response already received. For the coroutine case, pre-patch `await chain(request)` and post-patch `iscoroutine → await` yield the identical final response, so the actual user-facing issue (e.g. django-cors-headers getting a coroutine) is not resolved. Root cause fix belongs in MiddlewareMixin (awa

Runtime `asyncio.iscoroutine()` branch is a band-aid that papers over indeterminate async-ness of the middleware chain rather than guaranteeing the chain is properly adapted. get_response_async should know deterministically whether the chain is a coroutine; a type-sniffing conditional signals the middleware adaptation layer is the real defect site.
